# Tender market report: digital pre-operative assessment

**Date:** 2026-10-22. **Product:** Preopsis (repo `poised`). **Scope:** public tenders, awards, PINs, market engagements, framework listings and buyer evidence for digital pre-operative assessment and the modules buyers bundle with it (consent and shared decision-making, patient engagement and questionnaires, PROMs/PREMs, waiting-list validation, prehab/ERAS, remote monitoring, surgical scheduling, perioperative EPR modules) in the UK, Ireland and Europe, mostly notices from Oct 2023 to Oct 2026.

## 0. Date, scope and method

- **Agents:** 42 research runs: 18 area researchers (UK frameworks, Find a Tender, Contracts Finder, trust portals, consent, PROMs and remote monitoring, engagement, waiting list and prehab, devolved nations, Ireland, DACH, Netherlands/Belgium, Nordics, southern Europe, TED, competitors, compliance), 19 deep-read agents that opened notices and documents, and 5 gap-filling agents (England trust map, Ireland, devolved nations, France/Spain/Italy, renewal dates).
- **Sources:** Find a Tender (OCDS API), Contracts Finder (API), Public Contracts Scotland, Sell2Wales, eTendersNI, TED (API v3), Irish eTenders, TenderNed, BOSA/3P (Belgium), simap.ch, Doffin and Mercell, Tarjouspalvelu.fi, PLACSP and the Madrid portal, ANAC (Italy), DECP/BOAMP (France), BASE (Portugal), the G-Cloud Digital Marketplace, trust FOI logs, board papers and spend files, NHS England, GIRFT, DTAC, MHRA and EU regulation pages, and supplier websites.
- **Counts:** 370 tender records came in. For the tender table, duplicates of the same procurement were merged, 3 records that bundled several notices were split, and 9 clearly irrelevant ones were dropped (asset tracking, theatre equipment, generic IT frameworks), so 310 rows remain in section 2. The records hold 2,915 requirement statements. The research also logged 582 findings, 1,310 searches and 441 dead ends.
- **Complete feature mapping (new in this version):** all 2,915 statements were mapped one by one to a feature. The result is **625 features**: the 89 headline features from the first pass, plus **536 long-tail features** for specific asks the headline set did not cover. No statement was left unmapped. One statement can support more than one feature. 486 are product features and 139 are commercial or service terms. Every statement, with its tender and link, is in the appendix, [tender-research-appendix.md](tender-research-appendix.md), section A, under the feature id.
- **Supplier profiles (new):** the 466 competitor mentions were merged into **178 supplier profiles**, each with features, wins, accreditations, integrations and links. Appendix section B holds every profile. Sections 6b and 6c are generated from them.
- **Documents read:** full tender documents were read for 54 records; the rest rely on notice text, award data, FOIs and supplier pages. 182 records sit behind a gated portal (Atamis, 3P, eTenders, Mercell, Tarjouspalvelu and others) whose specifications were not read (section 8).
- **Demand counts:** "Tenders" is the number of distinct tender records that state a feature, split UK / Ireland / rest of Europe ("EU" means EU countries plus Switzerland and Norway). The count uses the records as found: 352 records carry at least one statement. A procurement published as several notices can count more than once (AZORG appears as 3 records and Mannheim as 2), so read the counts as relative demand, not exact totals. "Pre-op" counts how many of a feature's records are pre-op assessment records; 27 records with statements are pre-op records. Our status comes from the repo baseline; "Planned" counts as Missing and names the plan.
- **Priority (changed in this version):** priority now comes from demand only. **P1:** 20 or more tenders, or 3 or more pre-op tenders. **P2:** 5 or more tenders, or at least 1 pre-op tender. **P3:** the rest. **Have:** we already support it, so keep it and show it in demos. The earlier version also weighed gap size and sales impact and lifted assurance items to P1; that is dropped. Of the 486 product features, 27 are supported, 36 are P1 gaps, 83 are P2 gaps and 340 are P3 gaps. With commercial terms, there are 46 P1 gaps; section 1 covers all of them. Assurance items that are only P2 by tender count (DTAC, DSPT, DCB0129, Cyber Essentials) still gate NHS sales, because the trust specifications that would state them are mostly gated (section 5).
- **Limits:** most English trust specifications sit in Atamis and were not read, so tender text understates assurance and integration asks. Coverage is thin for Ireland (14 records), Northern Ireland (2 records), Scotland and Wales outside the national buys, Austria, Poland and Slovenia (1-4 records each), and southern Europe, where many buys are minor contracts. Dutch general hospitals are not bound by procurement law, so their pre-op buys do not appear on TenderNed. Values are often unpublished. Supplier claims (customer counts, savings) are vendor statements. A supplier profile lists only what its sources state, so a blank in sections 6b and 6c means "not found", not "not offered". Where a value or date is unknown the report says "not published".

## 1. Executive summary

Selling first: these are the things to build or prove to become the leading bid, **ranked by demand**. The lead number is how many tender records state the item's main feature, with the pre-op records among them in brackets (section 3). Each item names its feature ids. Together the 18 items cover **all 46 P1 gaps** in the backlog (36 product, 10 commercial). Some items have few tenders but many pre-op ones (triage, decision support, write-back, languages, device status). In a pre-op bid they matter more than their totals suggest.

1. **Set the price, licence and service model** (evidence: 131 tenders, 14 pre-op; status: Missing, Partial). Features: CM06 price and licence model, 131 (14); CM04 implementation, training and ongoing support, 115 (7); N427 perpetual licence option, 5 (3). Price is the most-stated ask in the whole data set. Royal Surrey's open ePOA tender weights commercial at 25%, equal to scripted demos. NHS Golden Jubilee's perioperative app split the award 60% quality and 40% price, and asked for monthly KPIs on uptime, response times and incidents. HeCaPP's Belgian anaesthesia software tender scored price 30, ease of use 30 and training 17. Some EU buyers want to own the licence: Mannheim bought a perpetual licence for its pre-op screening, and SESCAM bought perpetual consent licences. Published competitor prices set the range: Ultramed GBP 2.80-5.00 per submission, VitalHub GBP 2.90-3.50 per pre-op, Isla GBP 1.70 per appointment, Aire Logic from GBP 14,000 a year, Open Medical from GBP 48,500 a year. We have no price list, support model or service desk yet. Recommendation: publish a per-patient price and an annual enterprise tier, a support and training offer with service KPIs, and decide whether EU bids can get a perpetual licence. Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-06d687) [2](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/1380-2026) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/335020-2026/xml) [6](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-pricing-document-2026-01-15-1455.pdf) [7](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/721733/214669371000433-pricing-document-2026-01-29-1809.pdf) [8](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/715326/283818920610894-pricing-document-2026-01-30-1240.pdf) [9](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/722146/453946191700706-pricing-document-2026-01-29-1117.pdf) [10](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/706548/106177073699977-pricing-document-2026-01-29-0909.pdf)

2. **Integrate with the hospital's EPR, PAS and other systems** (evidence: 109 tenders, 11 pre-op; status: Missing). Features: IN01 bi-directional EPR/PAS integration, 109 (11); IN08 integration with other hospital systems (portal, AIMS, theatre, devices), 65 (2); IN05 write results and documents back to the EPR, 43 (8); IN03 FHIR and open APIs, 41 (2); IN09 shared care record and national data sets, 39 (4); IN02 HL7 v2, 30 (3). Also P2: IN04 demographics lookup, 17; IN07 staff single sign-on and EPR context launch, 14. Buyers want answers and documents to flow into the hospital record and demographics to flow out of it. In pre-op buys: AZORG wants answers stored in its KWS; NWAFT pays for POA outputs pushed into the trust record; Mannheim requires HL7 v2, FHIR and REST to SAP ISHmed and its patient portal; DHCW makes interoperability with NHS Wales systems a core requirement and wants structured data for national repositories; Golden Jubilee made HL7 v2.4 in and out a must-have. The incumbents already do this: HL7 v2.4 demographics query and document return (Ultramed), HL7/FHIR and JSON:API (Open Medical), EPR context launch in Epic and Cerner (Isla). Today this is out of scope by decision A-10. Recommendation: reverse A-10 and build an HL7 v2 demographics-in and PDF/structured-data-out pack first, then FHIR. This is our biggest single product gap. Sources: [1](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/702720-2026/xml) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [4](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021393-2026) [5](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [6](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf) [7](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/231234506205685) [8](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/283818920610894)

3. **Get on the buying routes before the next renewal wave** (evidence: 69 tenders, 9 pre-op, 58 of them UK; status: Missing). Features: CM01 framework or catalogue route, 69 (9); N421 direct award without competition, 17 (3). Every English pre-op purchase found was a framework call-off or direct award, mostly published after award (G-Cloud, CDHS, Digital Workplace Solutions 2 via Softcat, NHS SBS). Northumbria bought VitalHub as a framework call-off, and NWAFT direct-awarded Ultramed through Softcat. No English acute trust ran an open pre-op competition from Oct 2023 to Oct 2026 except Royal Surrey (2026). The patient-engagement frameworks are already set: NHS SBS SBS10521 (GBP 250m, to Feb 2030) lists DrDoctor, Netcall, Zesty, RIVIAM and Aire Logic among others in Lot 1, and NHS Commercial Solutions is replacing its GBP 1.4bn patient-communications framework. A G-Cloud 15 listing must describe data extraction at exit and declare ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials and social value commitments. Actions: list on G-Cloud (the G-Cloud 15 catalogue already lists more than ten pre-op and adjacent products); prepare for CDHS 2.0 (contract notice expected early 2027, live about Oct 2027); talk to resellers such as Softcat. Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ecfccd32-f3aa-4601-b26f-c29dc6ed5ed8) [3](https://www.publictechnology.net/?p=13604) [4](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/032423-2024) [5](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/214669371000433) [6](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/073826-2026) [7](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/028372-2026) [8](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4b01b246-d069-49ec-ab9a-d2be725791e1) [9](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/191971979468258)

4. **Offer digital consent with e-signature, through a partner** (evidence: 64 tenders, 2 pre-op; UK 14, EU 49; status: Missing). Feature: CW05 digital consent with electronic signature, 64 (2). Related P2 features: N025 digital admission paperwork, 8; N004 eIDAS-grade signatures, 6; PX13 shared decision-making tools, 6. Consent is the largest adjacent buying category. UK buys are stand-alone and mid-sized: Concentric at Barts (GBP 180,000), PAHT (GBP 190,000 via Softcat), Northumbria (GBP 300,000) and Buckinghamshire (GBP 210,000); EIDO at Barnsley (GBP 105,000). In Germany, Thieme's E-ConsentPro is bought under the Sana group framework (up to EUR 4.29m) and by Köln (EUR 883,780.91). In pre-op it is bundled: Mannheim pairs pre-op screening with video consent, and Open Medical's ePOA includes consent on the patient's device. We have a signature question type but no consent product. Recommendation: partner for consent content and legally valid signature (EIDO or Concentric in the UK, Thieme in DACH) and link it to the pre-op episode. Build only the hand-off. Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/6c82cb27-b277-42c4-b41f-8bb36547d70f) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/0d978ff9-f1e5-44a0-87c9-af3e7827f57d) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/013787-2025) [4](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/009469-2026) [5](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7af91ea8-535a-4bc8-a105-48829a293c57) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/254451-2024/xml) [7](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/131869-2025/xml) [8](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [9](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/231234506205685) [10](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063)

5. **Decide how to meet the patient-portal asks** (evidence: 59 tenders, 2 pre-op; status: Partial, Missing). Features: PX07 patient portal for appointments, letters, documents and results, 59 (2); PX10 digital letters and hybrid mail, 29 (0); PX02 mobile access or a native app, 26 (0); PX08 self-service booking and rescheduling, 26 (0); PX09 two-way messaging with the care team, 25 (2). Also P2: PX14 video consultation, 18 (2). These are what patient engagement platforms sell. Trusts often buy them as one portal contract, then run pre-op screening on it: DrDoctor won Warrington and Halton (GBP 2,235,865) and Lewisham and Greenwich (GBP 865,000), where pre-op forms reach the NHS App. Pre-op tenders also ask for some of it: Golden Jubilee made secure in-app chat a must-have, and a Welsh telehealth engagement lists two-way messaging. Two-way messaging is excluded for now by decision A-15. Section 1a below lists every engagement feature we lack, who sells it, and the strategic choice. Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/004133-2024) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/b62c55b2-5418-4845-9233-ad9840d42162) [3](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/eca89ee2-1071-4c83-8ddd-84fcb6af96fd) [4](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [5](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=JUL523762)

6. **Add patient education, a content library and a patient-facing language switch** (evidence: 58 tenders, 9 pre-op; status: Missing, Partial). Features: PX06 procedure information, videos, preparation and after-care content, 58 (9); PX04 multilingual content and local-language rules, 32 (8); QC04 ready-made clinical content library, 26 (0). Pre-op buyers ask for education: Golden Jubilee wanted pre-op education, a countdown to surgery and a packing checklist; NSS wanted patients supported about their procedure at set intervals; AZORG and Mannheim tie videos to the questionnaire; PAHT's ePOA includes education videos. Languages: Welsh notices require bilingual Welsh/English delivery; Mannheim wanted German, English, Arabic and French; AZORG wants questionnaires and videos in several languages. Content libraries are bought as products: EIDO's procedure leaflets at Shrewsbury (estimated GBP 80,000) and ULHT (GBP 129,130.27). Video and Information elements are planned in C5. Translations can be authored, but patients cannot switch language. The planned S24 question library is not a clinical content library. Recommendation: build the content player and the language switch (C5); license leaflet and consent content rather than write it. Sources: [1](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007268-2023) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/702720-2026/xml) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [5](https://www.pah.nhs.uk/?p=7047) [6](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=AUG535492) [7](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021282-2025) [8](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/df666f8b-808a-4f66-9e88-472dc2ba2ecb)

8. **Feed theatre scheduling and day-of-surgery systems; do not build them** (evidence: 54 tenders, 3 pre-op; UK 16, EU 36; status: Missing). Features: SW03 theatre and surgical scheduling, operating lists and waiting-list management, 54 (3); SW04 day-of-surgery coordination, patient flow and bed management, 26 (0; EU 22). Buyers link pre-op to theatre use. NSS's PIN bundled a national pre-op online triage with theatre scheduling, but only scheduling was bought (Infix, GBP 6.3m). NHS GGC is market-testing a theatre patient management system next to its digital pre-op PIN. A Welsh theatre management system engagement ran demos in Sep 2025. Portugal's ULS Alentejo bought day-surgery and pre-anaesthetic consultation software together (UpHill). Northumbria uses its pre-op tool to keep a pool of ready patients. Day-of-surgery coordination is a separate market, led by Germany (11 of its 26 tenders): sqior won Heidelberg (EUR 694,980), and Parc de Salut Mar in Barcelona bought real-time location tracking. We already track fitness for surgery. Recommendation: send a 'pre-op ready' pool to scheduling systems through the integration pack (item 2); partner, do not build. 10. **Meet national programme criteria, including 'waiting well'** (evidence: 41 tenders, 4 pre-op; status: Partial). Feature: CS11 national programme criteria (NHS England's five core requirements, GIRFT, KHZG), 41 (4). Related P2 features: SW01 patient-facing waiting-list validation, 15 (1; all UK); PF06 prehabilitation and ERAS, 18 (1); SW02 3-monthly re-contact while waiting, 5 (2). NHS England's five core requirements include contacting every inpatient waiter at least every three months and optimising at-risk patients, and the NHS Standard Contract (SC3.18) makes early screening and optimisation a contract duty for acute providers. Somerset aligned its pre-op tool with the five core requirements. Worcestershire's Ultramed system re-contacts patients every 3 months until a date is set. Netcall sells waiting-list validation (NHS Devon GBP 132,195; County Durham and Darlington GBP 46,895), and Zesty sells its form builder for both pre-op and validation. German portal buys must meet the KHZG FTB 2 must-criteria (Köln). Our reminders and pre-fill (C4) are the base for this. 11. **Collect PROMs (plan C9); partner for registry upload; PREMs later** (evidence: 41 tenders, 2 pre-op; UK 26; status: Missing). Features: PF01 PROMs before and after surgery, 41 (2); PF02 PREMs and patient-experience surveys, 21 (0); PF03 submission to national registries, 20 (0). Also P2: N142 Friends and Family Test, 7. Golden Jubilee wanted PROMs pre-op and at set post-op points, and Somerset collects post-op outcomes in its pre-op tool. The big buys are national or regional: NHS England's registries platform (NEC, GBP 4.16m transition contract to Sep 2027), the All Wales PROMs framework (GBP 11.9m), Region Skåne's PROM/PREM tool (Stretch, up to SEK 65m) and Helsinki's 34 quality registries (BCB Medical, EUR 4.3m). Registry upload is the barrier to entry: Royal Berkshire direct-awarded Amplitude because no one else had proven NJR and multi-registry upload. Sources: [1](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [2](https://www.somersetft.nhs.uk/about-us/wp-content/uploads/sites/148/2024/02/Strategy-and-Planning-Monday-19-February-2024.pdf) [3](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9) [4](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/032382-2023) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/10140-2025) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/279840-2026) [7](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/044783-2026)

12. **Clear the NHS assurance and security bar: DTAC, DCB0129, DSPT, Cyber Essentials, pen test, then ISO 27001** (evidence: 40 tenders, 2 pre-op; status: Partial, Missing). Features: CS09 security controls (MFA, encryption, roles, audit logs, pen testing), 40 (2); CS01 GDPR, DPIA and data processing agreement, 36 (5); HD08 scale at regional or national volumes, 25 (3); CS02 ISO 27001, 21 (5); HD04 availability SLA, backup and disaster recovery, 21 (1). By tender count the named NHS items are only P2: CS03 Cyber Essentials, 13; CS04 DSPT, 8; CS06 DCB0129, 6; CS05 DTAC, 5. But trust specifications are mostly gated, so tender counts understate them. DTAC v2.0 replaced v1.0, and suppliers must use it from 6 Apr 2026. Its pass/fail parts need a DCB0129 safety case and named Clinical Safety Officer, DSPT 'Standards Met', a Cyber Essentials certificate, a pen test within 12 months and NHS Number/PDS use. Golden Jubilee listed role-based access, encryption, audit logs, retention rules, MFA and security audits, plus its own DPIA template; LUMC wants availability above 99.5%; NSS's national scheduling buy was sized for 381 theatres. Most pre-op competitors on G-Cloud 15 advertise ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials Plus, many also DSPT and DCB0129, and Mannheim, Golden Jubilee and NHS Scotland's theatre tender asked for ISO 27001. Plan C10 covers DCB0129, DSPT, Cyber Essentials Plus, the pen test and backups; DTAC and ISO 27001 have no plan yet. Sources: [1](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx) [2](https://innovation.nhs.uk/news/updated-nhs-england-digital-technology-assessment-criteria-dtac-form-and-guidance/) [3](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/433084683660941) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [5](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [6](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/422834) [7](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAR473603) [8](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-03b258)

13. **Put the questionnaire in the NHS App and support NHS login** (evidence: 36 tenders, 3 pre-op; 28 of them UK; status: Missing). Features: IN06 national patient app and identity (NHS App, NHS login, Wayfinder, HSE App, MyCare.scot, DigiD), 36 (3). Also P2: N320 letters and appointments shown in the NHS App, 5. NHS England's Medium Term Planning Framework says patients must be able to receive and complete pre- and post-appointment questionnaires through the NHS App by the end of 2028/29. Princess Alexandra's portal is reached through the NHS App, Lewisham and Greenwich's pre-op forms reach the NHS App through DrDoctor, and Medway plans to onboard patients to the NHS App. Scotland's national MSK tender requires compatibility with MyCare.scot. DTAC v2.0 says patient-facing products should use NHS login. NHS login integration is free and takes about 3 to 4 months. Neither is planned today. Sources: [1](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/medium-term-planning-framework-delivering-change-together-2026-27-to-2028-29/) [2](https://healthcareleadernews.com/news/majority-of-appointments-to-be-available-on-nhs-app-from-april/) [3](https://www.pah.nhs.uk/news/the-princess-alexandra-hospital-100th-acute-nhs-trust-to-integrate-patient-portal-into-nhs-app/) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/eca89ee2-1071-4c83-8ddd-84fcb6af96fd) [5](https://www.medway.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/trust-board-in-public-may-2026-papers.pdf) [6](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT566180) [7](https://digital.nhs.uk/binaries/content/assets/website-assets/services/dtac/dtac_form_2.0_february_2026.docx) [8](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/nhs-login/nhs-login-for-partners-and-developers) [9](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/patient-care-aggregator/integrating-a-secondary-care-booking-system)

14. **Win the scored demo and land a first reference site** (evidence: 35 tenders, 4 pre-op; status: Missing, Partial). Features: CM02 references from live use at comparable hospitals, 35 (4); CM05 scored live or scripted demonstration, 17 (6). Royal Surrey's open ePOA tender gave scripted demonstrations 25% of the score, equal to price. AZORG scores a live demo and wants 2 to 5 references from the last three years. Golden Jubilee scored on-site use cases, such as turning a smoking page into a smoking/vaping questionnaire without the supplier. A Welsh theatre-system engagement ran demos by 4 to 6 shortlisted suppliers. Our authoring tool fits this demo well. We need one live NHS site: candidates without a digital pre-op tool are Dudley (plans one), East Sussex (none in Oct 2025), Sherwood Forest (paper) and Medway (board plan). 15. **Prepare the company paperwork once** (evidence: 25 tenders, 5 pre-op; status: Missing, Partial). Features: CM03 financial standing and insurance, 25 (5); CM09 social value, carbon reduction and fair work, 22 (4); CM08 procurement declarations (ESPD, exclusion grounds, e-invoicing), 16 (3). Golden Jubilee required GBP 5m employer's liability and GBP 2m professional indemnity cover, turnover of at least twice the contract value, and ISO 14001. AZORG requires an Altman Z-score above 1.5, an ESPD declaration and a 3% performance bond. Royal Surrey weights social value at 10%, and a G-Cloud 15 listing must give social value commitments. This is company work, not product work. 16. **Finish the clinician assessment record; integrate with, do not build, the anaesthesia record** (evidence: 21 tenders, 0 pre-op for AIMS; 20 tenders, 4 pre-op for clinician documentation; status: Missing, Partial). Features: N255 intra-operative anaesthesia record (AIMS), 21 (0; EU 18); CW03 pre-anaesthesia and nurse assessment documentation, 20 (4). Pre-op buyers want the clinician side, not just the questionnaire: Mannheim wanted 'the full pre-operative patient evaluation, from data capture to the medical decision'; HeCaPP's anaesthesia software tender (ICARE, EUR 1,067,966) required pre-op examination findings; ULS Alentejo bought pre-anaesthetic consultation software. AIMS buys are spread across Europe (Finland 4; Spain, Italy and Germany 3 each; only 2 in the UK) and sit next to the EPR: SERIS (Telefónica, EUR 565,673), Ramón y Cajal (MEDLINETEC) and Aragón's surgical process system (DH Healthcare). Capture blocks (C5) and observations (C7) are planned. Recommendation: complete CW03 in C5 and C7; leave AIMS to partners and integrate. 17. **Ship automated triage and decision support (plan C6) with validated scores (plan C7)** (evidence: 19 tenders, 9 pre-op; status: Partial). Features: TR01 automated risk stratification and triage, 19 (9); TR02 suggested next steps, tests and work-up plan, 18 (8). Also P2: TR06 AI or predictive models, 18 (1); TR04 modifiable risk factors and optimisation referral, 8 (2); TR03 ASA grade and validated scores, 5. These two features have the highest pre-op share of any gap: pre-op buyers ask the system to sort patients, not just collect answers. DHCW wants risk stratification to choose the right site; NSS wanted a national pre-op online triage; Somerset reports risk-stratified screening with 67% completion; AZORG wants the system to map the work-up plan per patient; Medway wants fewer repeat pre-op tests. NHS England's five core requirements and the GIRFT POA guidance expect early screening and triage. Competitors sell this hard: Synopsis claims 250+ algorithms (ASA, STOP-BANG, P-POSSUM, frailty), and Ultramed derives ASA, frailty and suggested tasks. 18. **Decide the medical-device route before shipping auto-triage** (evidence: 15 tenders, 4 pre-op; status: Missing). Feature: CS07 medical device status and certification, 15 (4). MHRA guidance says software that triages, scores risk or predicts is likely a medical device; under EU MDR Rule 11 decision-support software is usually class IIa. Mannheim bought a medical device product, Golden Jubilee asked bidders to declare device status, Aragón's surgical system is CE-marked Class I, and LUMC and the HSE ask for MDR evidence. Ultramed and VitalHub say they are MHRA-registered or CE-marked, Remcare claims UKCA Class I, and myPatientSpace says it is registered as a device in the EU. Our plan C6 (auto-triage) will cross this line, and the baseline has no device plan. ### 1a. What patient engagement platforms such as DrDoctor sell that we lack

**The point the data shows: we often compete against a portal, not a pre-op product.**

- **DrDoctor wins whole-portal contracts.** Warrington and Halton bought a patient engagement portal for GBP 2,235,865 (bi-directional EPR interface, NHS App and NHS login). Lewisham and Greenwich bought a patient portal for GBP 865,000 (2023-28). Others: Greater Manchester Mental Health GBP 572,527.90, Bradford digital and hybrid letters GBP 513,151.95, UHB for the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital (GBP 207,424) and Birmingham Women's and Children's (GBP 323,771), and NHS England's Clinical Smart Forms pilot (GBP 348,000 plus GBP 75,000). DrDoctor says it serves 70+ trusts and boards. [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/004133-2024) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/b62c55b2-5418-4845-9233-ad9840d42162) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/011476-2025) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/d3d2477b-a5ec-423e-bef9-c7444e14cd14) [5](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/10a25532-80f3-436c-900a-debe0d1b54f5) [6](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/1361d99a-7b9e-49d5-a2f3-ce5304b274ea)
- **Its pre-op cost is bundled and cannot be separated.** Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh said in an FOI that its pre-op questionnaire sits inside the wider DrDoctor contract and the cost cannot be split out. Salisbury withheld the value as not specific to pre-op. None of DrDoctor's tender notices names pre-op; its pre-op use shows only in trust pages and FOIs. [1](https://www.wwl.nhs.uk/media/FOI/202526/04%20-%20July%202025/10899%20-%20Use%20of%20Digital%20Pre-operative%20Assessment%20Solutions.pdf) [2](https://www.salisbury.nhs.uk/about-us/freedom-of-information-foi/previous-foi-requests/foi_8903/)
- **Trusts run pre-op screening on it.** Norfolk and Norwich runs digital pre-op pre-screening on DrDoctor and resends the questionnaire every 3 months while patients wait. Salisbury and Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh use it for pre-op too, and Moorfields for its digital questionnaire. Lewisham and Greenwich patients complete pre-op forms in the NHS App through DrDoctor (from Sep 2025). [1](https://www.nnuh.nhs.uk/departments/pre-admission-assessment/pre-screening/) [2](https://www.salisbury.nhs.uk/about-us/freedom-of-information-foi/previous-foi-requests/foi_8903/) [3](https://www.wwl.nhs.uk/media/FOI/202526/04%20-%20July%202025/10899%20-%20Use%20of%20Digital%20Pre-operative%20Assessment%20Solutions.pdf) [4](https://moorfields.nhs.uk/for-patients/plan-your-visit/digital-questionnaire) [5](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/eca89ee2-1071-4c83-8ddd-84fcb6af96fd)
- **Other portals do the same.** Patients Know Best runs a digital pre-assessment pathway in Hull and Humber and North Yorkshire (GBP 669,927, 2025-27) and the pre-op questionnaire at Dartford and Gravesham, via PKB or the NHS App. Zesty's Form Builder is sold for pre-op, PROMs, PREMs, consent and waiting-list validation, and Zesty is now part of VitalHub with Synopsis pre-op. Health Call's NHS App-native portal attaches pre-assessment questionnaires to appointments. Isla (listed as a pre-op specialist in 6c) sells a wider pathway platform: green-light pre-op triage plus post-op monitoring and PROMs, with 57% fewer on-the-day cancellations reported at Chelsea and Westminster. [1](https://patientsknowbest.com/huth/) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/0f5ef215-7ef1-4a61-8949-a79951e968b0) [3](https://www.dgt.nhs.uk/patients-and-visitors/outpatients-transformation/pkb/preparing-surgery-completing-your-online-pre-operative-questionnaire) [4](https://www.inductionhealthcare.com/capabilities/questionnaires) [5](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/721814/661878188565591-service-definition-document-2026-01-30-1234.pdf) [6](https://htn.co.uk/2026/03/10/scaling-clinical-excellence-and-efficiency-lessons-from-chelsea-and-westminster-nhs-foundation-trust/)
- **The portal market is large and framework-led.** Healthcare Communications (IMImobile/Cisco) won Frimley (GBP 3m) and Isle of Wight (GBP 412,808); Wellola won Lincolnshire (GBP 1,084,550); Patients Know Best won UH Sussex (GBP 1,163,190); Netcall's Patient Hub runs at East and North Herts and NHS Highland. Hampshire and Isle of Wight estimated GBP 800,000 for a portal with cohort notifications. Most buys are call-offs from NHS SBS SBS10521 (GBP 250m) or NHS Commercial Solutions. [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/09fe575a-2628-4553-9214-6c5243bea58f) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/006421-2024) [3](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/63a98bff-7214-4276-9292-052bdb0c4c75) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/54fa4b5d-1269-4978-99b4-9252204b043a) [5](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/f134a186-463a-4202-9b0c-dfe5fdffa9ac) [6](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=JAN546569) [7](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/041626-2024) [8](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/028372-2026)
- **Portals churn, which opens doors.** Royal Berkshire replaced DrDoctor with its own 'Royal Berkshire Connect'; Birmingham Women's and Children's moved to Epic MyChart; WWL's DrDoctor contract expired in Oct 2025 and was 'under review'; Hertfordshire Partnership replaced IMImobile with Patients Know Best in 2026; Bradford's GBP 10.18m joint portal tender was cancelled in Jan 2026. We already match them on the core of a pre-op form: remote questionnaires, SMS and email reminders, configurable forms with branching and scores, clinician worklists and a secure link with a date-of-birth check. They also hold the framework places (CM01: all of the UK platforms above) and the NHS assurance pack: DrDoctor declares a DTAC pass, DSPT 'Standards Exceeded', DCB0129, ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials Plus. Sources: [1](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/606705557370842) [2](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/505878518749739) [3](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/731883939256464) [4](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/859745589024317) [5](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/751087773918162) [6](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/458593140129064)

**The strategic choice (recommendation; Rahul decides).**

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Plug into existing portals (recommended)** | Stay the pre-op specialist. Make the questionnaire, triage and clinical review reachable from the NHS App through NHS login and Wayfinder. Offer a FHIR assessment API so a trust's portal or EPR can launch our forms and receive answers and scores. Add only the engagement pieces a pre-op journey needs. | Most trusts already own a portal, so we sell alongside it, not against it. The NHS App is the national direction for questionnaires by 2028/29. DrDoctor already writes assessments back through a FHIR Digital Assessment API, so the pattern exists. Some EU buyers already ask for forms inside their existing portal (N288: Basel, Halle, AGAPLESION, 4 tenders). | We depend on portal suppliers who may sell their own pre-op forms. Portal contracts that bundle pre-op stay closed to us until they renew. |
| B. Build a full portal | Add letters, hybrid mail, booking, video and broad messaging. | Lets us bid for whole-portal contracts (GBP 0.1m to 3m). | Head-on with DrDoctor, PKB, Zesty, Netcall and HCUK, who hold the SBS10521 framework places to 2030. Needs PAS booking write-back and print partners. Pulls us away from the pre-op depth that wins pre-op tenders. |
| C. Be a portal's pre-op module | Resell or white-label through one portal supplier. | Fast reach into their trusts. | Ties us to one channel; VitalHub already pairs Zesty with Synopsis. |

Under option A, the engagement pieces worth adding first, by demand: patient education and preparation content (PX06, 58 tenders, 9 pre-op; C5); NHS App and NHS login (IN06, 36); FHIR and HL7 interfaces (IN03 41, IN02 30) as the 'plug'; PROMs and recovery check-ins (PF01, 41; C9); two-way messaging limited to the pre-op team (PX09, 25; needs a change to A-15); photo and document upload (PX12, 10; C8); 3-monthly re-contact and waiting-list validation (SW02 5, SW01 15). Leave letters, hybrid mail, booking and video to the portal. Sources: [1](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/medium-term-planning-framework-delivering-change-together-2026-27-to-2028-29/) [2](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/606705557370842) [3](https://www.simap.ch/api/publications/v1/project/29e09e7b-d943-4cfc-9a8a-38d82109405e/publication-details/ab028b14-b6f9-4d45-bfa4-7893418f4ba5) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/851883-2025/xml) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/382793-2024/xml) [6](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/028372-2026) [7](https://digital.nhs.uk/services/patient-care-aggregator/integrating-a-secondary-care-booking-system)

## 3. Complete feature backlog, ranked by demand

This is every feature buyers asked for in the tenders found: **625 features** from all 2,915 requirement statements. Each statement was mapped one by one. The 89 headline features come from the first pass, and 536 more come from the long tail of specific asks. Nothing was dropped. Statements that matched no feature: 0.

- **Tenders** is the number of distinct tenders that state the feature. **Pre-op** counts how many of those are pre-op assessment tenders. **UK / IE / EU** splits the tenders by market (EU includes Switzerland and Norway).
- **Priority comes from demand only.** P1 means 20 or more tenders, or 3 or more pre-op tenders. P2 means 5 or more tenders, or at least one pre-op tender. P3 is everything else. **Have** means we already support it, so keep it and show it in demos. Gated English specifications were not read, so assurance and integration asks are undercounted (section 0).
- **Work** is the type of work needed: the main bucket in bold, then the others it also needs. Section 3d groups the backlog by bucket, so non-coding work (clinical, assurance, commercial, service, partner deals) can run in parallel with development. The buckets were assigned by reading each feature and its tender asks; treat them as a first cut to adjust.
- **Suppliers offering it** lists the competitors whose profile states the feature (appendix B). It is filled for the headline features; for long-tail features, see the supplier profiles.
- **Decision** is blank for Rahul: build now, later, partner, or no.
- The evidence for every row (each statement, its tender and its link) is in [the appendix](tender-research-appendix.md), section A, under the same feature id.

Product features: 486. Already supported: 27. P1 gaps: 36. P2 gaps: 83. P3 gaps: 340.

### 3d. Backlog by type of work

Every gap (product and commercial; features we already support are left out) appears once, under its **main** bucket, ranked by demand. **Also needs** lists the other buckets it touches. Read it to see what can start now without code: the clinical, assurance, commercial and partner tables can be worked by a clinician, consultant or partner while development continues.

| **Build** | Code we write in Preopsis. | Developer | 169 | 12 | 32 | 125 | 305 |

| **Clinical** | Clinician time, little or no code: content, validated scoring rules, clinical safety case, pathway design. | Contracted clinician or Clinical Safety Officer | 56 | 5 | 13 | 38 | 168 |
| **Assurance** | Certification, audits and compliance paperwork. | Compliance consultant or auditor | 42 | 3 | 9 | 30 | 124 |

| **Service** | Delivering to customers: implementation, training, support, SLA, migration. | Implementation and support staff | 41 | 2 | 10 | 29 | 92 |
| **Partner** | Best bought, resold or integrated from a specialist partner rather than built. | Partnership deal | 99 | 7 | 15 | 77 | 146 |

## 4. Recommended suite

Every module-sized gap, ranked by demand. **Summed demand** adds up the tender counts of the module's features from section 3, so a tender that asks for three of the features counts three times. **Distinct records** counts each tender once. Pre-op is summed the same way. Recommendations are build, partner or integrate; Rahul decides. Integration, triage and the NHS App are core to pre-op rather than add-on modules; they are listed so the ranking is complete, and section 1 covers them in detail.

**What buyers bundle each module with.** The bundles below come from which modules appear together in the same tender records (shared record counts in brackets), plus the examples cited.

1. **Integration (summed 378; build).** Integration appears in more tenders than any module, and every other module is bundled with it: patient portal (60 shared records), education (57), reporting (50), consent (41). Suppliers that state it: Isla, Open Medical, Ultramed, VitalHub, Aire Logic, Rumi, NovaCair, DrDoctor, Zesty, Thieme, EIDO, Concentric and sqior. See section 1 item 2 for the build order. Sources: [1](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/283818920610894) [2](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-service-definition-document-2025-12-18-1101.pdf) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml)

2. **Patient portal and communications (summed 191; integrate, build only the pre-op pieces).** Portals are bought as whole-portal contracts worth GBP 0.1m to 3m, mostly from NHS SBS SBS10521 or NHS Commercial Solutions. Suppliers: DrDoctor, Patients Know Best, Zesty (VitalHub), Netcall, Healthcare Communications (IMImobile/Cisco), Wellola, Health Call, RIVIAM and Synertec in the UK; Doctolib, POLAVIS, m.Doc, PLANFOX and samedi in Germany; Mehiläinen in Finland. *Bundled with:* integration (60), education (27), the NHS App (21) and waiting-list validation (20); hybrid mail is often in the same tender (Bradford, Lincolnshire). Section 1a gives the feature-by-feature view and the strategic choice. Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/028372-2026) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/004133-2024) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-0523c3) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/63a98bff-7214-4276-9292-052bdb0c4c75) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/103330-2025/xml)

3. **Patient education, preparation content and languages (summed 120, 20 pre-op; build the player, license content).** The most pre-op-heavy add-on. AZORG and Mannheim tie videos to the pre-op questionnaire; the Golden Jubilee perioperative app wanted a countdown, packing checklists and push reminders; PAHT's ePOA includes education videos. Content is sold by EIDO (procedure leaflets) and Thieme (consent forms with videos in 20 languages); NovaCair, Buddy, DrDoctor, Wellola, Doctolib, Zimmer and ikHerstel bundle content in their apps. *Bundled with:* integration (57), consent (38) and the portal (27). Video and Information elements are planned in C5. Sources: [1](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/702720-2026) [2](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [3](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [4](https://www.pah.nhs.uk/?p=7047) [5](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021282-2025) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/672595-2024/xml)

4. **Digital consent and shared decision-making (summed 106; partner).** The largest adjacent buying category. In pre-op it is bundled: Open Medical's ePOA includes consent on the patient's device, GIRFT's low-risk ePOA model includes digital consent, NovaCair and Mannheim pair screening with video consent, and South Tees ran an open consent and SDM tender (GBP 135,018). Suppliers: EIDO and Concentric (UK), Thieme (DACH; over 90% share per one buyer), Plexus (Spain), Docaposte and DrData (France), Cinnamon and MD Consents (UK niche). EIDO markets integration with pre-op systems, so a content partnership is a fast route. Content libraries lock buyers in (Thieme in Germany), so partner rather than write content. *Bundled with:* integration (41), education and leaflets (38), the portal (19), e-signature and EPR document filing. Sources: [1](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/231234506205685) [2](https://gettingitrightfirsttime.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/GIRFT-Pre-operative-assessment-guidance-FINAL-V1-July-2023.pdf) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719) [5](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/572022146131063) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/238918-2024/xml) [7](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/335020-2026/xml)

5. **PROMs, PREMs and registries (summed 102; build PROMs in C9, partner for registries).** NHS England's national PROMs and registries platform is on a transition contract to Sep 2027 with a replacement planned; the All Wales PROMs framework reaches its maximum term around Oct 2027. Open Medical and VitalHub already sell both pre-op and PROMs. The barrier is registry upload: Royal Berkshire direct-awarded Amplitude because no one else had proven NJR and multi-registry upload. Suppliers: NEC, Amplitude, Aire Logic, My Clinical Outcomes, Promptly, Quality Health, Pro-Mapp (UK); BCB Medical (Finland), Stretch (Sweden), dotbase (Germany), SKEZI (France). *Bundled with:* integration (35), reporting and outcome dashboards (26) and the portal (14); Somerset collects post-op outcomes in its pre-op tool. Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/032382-2023) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/044783-2026) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/1c16e332-f07c-4e99-b288-ff1e68cf56e1) [5](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/106177073699977) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/279840-2026) [7](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/10140-2025)

6. **Reporting, analytics and data export (summed 98; build).** Buyers want dashboards, KPIs, audit and benchmarking data, and a clean exit. DHCW wants structured data for audit and national repositories; every G-Cloud 15 listing must describe end-of-contract data extraction. Suppliers that state it: Open Medical, Ultramed, VitalHub, Aire Logic, Rumi (Power BI export), Netcall, NEC, Amplitude, Trisoft, Infix, sqior, MBI Health, C2-Ai, Encare (ERAS audit). *Bundled with:* integration (50), PROMs (26), scheduling (22) and education (23). Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021393-2026) [2](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/191971979468258) [3](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/433084683660941) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/509259-2026)

7. **Remote monitoring, virtual wards and wearables (summed 91; partner).** A separate market led by Doccla in the UK and bought through frameworks such as TECS2. LUMC wants care paths that switch from pre-op to post-op on a schedule, and the Golden Jubilee app wanted post-op exercise videos, wound photos and wearable data. Suppliers: Doccla, Whzan, Inhealthcare, Docobo, Huma and the other TECS2 suppliers (UK); Calmedica (France); Cambio and Cuviva (Sweden); Luscii, ikHerstel (Netherlands); myPatientSpace (Ireland); Hope Care (Portugal). *Bundled with:* integration (27), the portal (20), reporting (16), education (16), device logistics and PROMs. Sources: [1](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/408350/documenten/13575475/content) [2](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959) [3](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/39dc6b3f-5320-4b0a-9705-3a7cf94f4880) [4](https://htn.co.uk/2023/03/27/nhs-sbs-updates-remote-patient-monitoring-procurement-framework/) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/374454-2025/html)

8. **Day-of-surgery flow, patient tracking and OR coordination (summed 88, 1 pre-op; partner or leave).** Almost no pre-op overlap. German university hospitals buy sqior's OR coordination assistant by repeated direct award (Heidelberg EUR 694,980; LMU, Bonn, MHH, Erlangen); Spanish hospitals buy location tracking (Telefónica at Parc de Salut Mar, IMPEMER at Parc Taulí, MySphera at Moisès Broggi); Västra Götaland bought regional patient-flow software (Axel Health). *Bundled with:* integration (29), theatre scheduling (18) and the portal (16). Sources: [1](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/346080-2025) [2](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/300707-2026) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/414800-2025/xml) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/167950-2025/xml) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/646465-2024)

9. **Theatre and surgical scheduling (summed 76; integrate).** Buyers link pre-op to theatre use: NSS bundled national pre-op triage with theatre scheduling (only scheduling was bought, from Infix), Northumbria uses its pre-op tool to keep a pool of ready patients, and GIRFT asks for a ready-list. Integrate rather than build a scheduler. Suppliers: Infix and Trisoft (UK), Bluespier and the EPR theatre modules, MBI Health (LUNA), Tetra AI, CIRUS (Spain), G.I.S.O. and SurgiQ (Italy), UpHill (Portugal), Asseco (Poland). *Bundled with:* integration (27), reporting (22), the anaesthesia record (20) and day-of-surgery flow (18). Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007268-2023) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/017154-2024) [3](https://www.northumbria.nhs.uk/media-centre/news-and-blogs/news-stories/northumbria-healthcare-launches-digital-pre-operative-assessments-optimise-theatre-use) [4](https://gettingitrightfirsttime.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/GIRFT-Pre-operative-assessment-guidance-FINAL-V1-July-2023.pdf) [5](https://www.trisoft.co.uk/) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/368907-2026/xml)

10. **Triage, decision support and AI (summed 73, 24 pre-op; build).** The module with the highest pre-op share. Suppliers: Ultramed, VitalHub (250+ algorithms), Open Medical, Aire Logic (AI ASA and mortality prediction), Isla, NovaCair, Rumi, Pro-Mapp, NEC, C2-Ai (risk stratification across Cheshire and Merseyside) and the EPR-native tools. *Bundled with:* integration (36), reporting (20) and education (20). Plans C6 and C7; see section 1 items 17 and 18 for the device question. Sources: [1](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/721733/214669371000433-service-definition-document-2026-01-29-1636.pdf) [2](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/92395/546146788659434-service-definition-document-2026-01-27-1259.pdf) [3](https://cheshireandmerseyside.nhs.uk/posts/region-wide-ai-deal-to-help-tackle-waiting-lists-across-nine-nhs-trusts)

11. **Anaesthesia record (AIMS), clinician documentation and ICU (summed 63; build CW03 only, integrate with AIMS).** The pre-op part (nurse and anaesthetist assessment, CW03) is asked for in 4 pre-op tenders and is planned in C5 and C7. The intra-operative record is a different product, bought next to the EPR: ICARE (HeCaPP, Belgium, EUR 1,067,966), MEDLINETEC (Ramón y Cajal), Telefónica (SERIS), DH Healthcare (Aragón), MEDLINQ, Systematic and Dedalus. *Bundled with:* integration (29), scheduling (20) and reporting (19). Sources: [1](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/1380-2026) [2](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/medias/anonmemoriaexp20244000140pdf/download) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/736459-2024/xml) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/52876-2025/html)

12. **Waiting well: 3-monthly recall, waiting-list validation and prehab (summed 62, 9 pre-op; build the recall, partner for prehab).** NHS England's core requirements (3-monthly contact, optimisation) and the 2025/26 guidance (validate waiters every 12 weeks with digital tools) create steady demand. NENC is planning a Waiting Well programme (contract notice estimated Apr 2027), and C2-Ai risk stratification feeds prehab across Cheshire and Merseyside. Suppliers: Ultramed (MyPreOp+ recall), Isla; for validation Netcall, DrDoctor, Zesty, Patients Know Best, Health Call and Healthcare Communications; for prehab Surgery Hero, PreActiv, QuestPrehab, Pro-Mapp and local waiting-well services. *Bundled with:* the portal (20), integration (20), the NHS App (16) and remote monitoring (15). Our reminders and pre-fill (C4) are the base. Sources: [1](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/earlier-screening-risk-assessment-and-health-optimisation-in-perioperative-pathways/) [2](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/2025-26-priorities-and-operational-planning-guidance/) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/073708-2026) [4](https://cheshireandmerseyside.nhs.uk/posts/region-wide-ai-deal-to-help-tackle-waiting-lists-across-nine-nhs-trusts) [5](https://www.inductionhealthcare.com/capabilities/questionnaires) [6](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c) [7](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/005813-2026)

13. **National app and identity (summed 41; build).** Patient engagement portals and a few pre-op tools already connect: DrDoctor, Patients Know Best, Zesty, Health Call, Netcall, Healthcare Communications, Isla and Rumi; Accenture, BJSS, Kainos and TPP build the national services. *Bundled with:* integration (25), the portal (21) and waiting well (16). See section 1 item 13. Sources: [1](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/medium-term-planning-framework-delivering-change-together-2026-27-to-2028-29/) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/74d58a5c-30ca-484a-a05e-a62084417228) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/006603-2026)

#### By competitor type

The table above covers the suppliers we meet most. Below is a short read of each type: who leads, where they win, and what they offer that we do not. Section 6b shows which suppliers cover our most-demanded gaps, section 6c lists all 178 suppliers by type, and appendix B has every profile.

- **Pre-op specialists (10 in 6c).** In the UK, Ultramed (Worcestershire GBP 240,000, NWAFT, UH Dorset, QEH King's Lynn, Tayside, Grampian, Cork) and Open Medical (PAHT, Somerset, West Herts) lead, with VitalHub Synopsis at Northumbria and NHS Highland, Isla selling through G-Cloud, and Aire Logic at Leeds. In Europe, NovaCair leads in the Netherlands and won Mannheim, and UpHill holds Portuguese perioperative contracts by renewal. They win framework call-offs and direct awards of about GBP 50k to 240k per trust. They offer what we lack: live EPR integration (IN01, IN05), a full NHS assurance pack and device registration (CS02, CS07), validated triage algorithms (TR01, TR02), BI (CW07), 3-monthly recall (SW02) and PROMs (PF01). Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/1c16e332-f07c-4e99-b288-ff1e68cf56e1) [3](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ecfccd32-f3aa-4601-b26f-c29dc6ed5ed8) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml) [5](https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=15610948)
- **Patient engagement platforms (25).** DrDoctor leads in England (Warrington and Halton GBP 2.24m, Lewisham and Greenwich GBP 865,000), followed by Patients Know Best (UH Sussex GBP 1.16m, Humber and North Yorkshire GBP 669,927), Healthcare Communications (Frimley GBP 3m), Wellola (Lincolnshire GBP 1.08m), Zesty (now VitalHub), Netcall (England and Scotland) and Health Call (owned by Northumbria Healthcare NHS FT). Doctolib, m.Doc, samedi, POLAVIS and PLANFOX sell KHZG-funded portals in Germany. They win whole-portal contracts, mostly as call-offs from NHS SBS SBS10521 and NHS Commercial Solutions, and several trusts run pre-op screening inside them with a cost that cannot be split out. They offer portal, letters and hybrid mail, booking, messaging, video, NHS App and NHS login, FHIR and HL7 write-back, PROMs and waiting-list validation. Section 1a has the feature list and the strategic choice. Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/004133-2024) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/54fa4b5d-1269-4978-99b4-9252204b043a) [3](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/09fe575a-2628-4553-9214-6c5243bea58f) [4](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/63a98bff-7214-4276-9292-052bdb0c4c75) [5](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/028372-2026) [6](https://www.wwl.nhs.uk/media/FOI/202526/04%20-%20July%202025/10899%20-%20Use%20of%20Digital%20Pre-operative%20Assessment%20Solutions.pdf) [7](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/103330-2025/xml)
- **Consent (14).** EIDO (16 wins found: NUH, Manchester, Barnsley, ULHT, Shrewsbury) and Concentric (Barts, PAHT, Northumbria, Buckinghamshire) lead in the UK. Thieme leads in Germany (13 wins, including the Sana framework up to EUR 4.29m and Köln EUR 883,780.91), and Plexus in Spain (SESCAM EUR 596,123.51). They win stand-alone consent buys and extensions of existing consent systems. They offer validated consent and leaflet libraries, legally valid e-signature and EPR document filing (CW05, QC04, N013), none of which we have. Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/bff5a924-895a-42b6-ae71-99b815e69b36) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/013787-2025) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/254451-2024/xml) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/131869-2025/xml) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/335020-2026/xml)
- **PROMs (13).** NEC runs NHS England's outcomes and registries platform (GBP 4.16m transition contract). Amplitude leads orthopaedic PROMs with registry upload (Royal Berkshire, West Suffolk, Somerset, ROH). Aire Logic, My Clinical Outcomes and Promptly share the All Wales PROMs framework. Abroad, BCB Medical runs Helsinki's 34 registries, Stretch won Region Skåne and dotbase won Charité's FHIR PROMs platform. They win national, regional and specialty contracts. They offer registry submission (PF03), PREMs (PF02) and outcome reporting that we lack. Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/044783-2026) [3](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/032382-2023) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/279840-2026) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/525437-2026)
- **Remote monitoring (19).** Doccla leads UK virtual wards (13 wins found, including Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB GBP 1.28m, South West London GBP 1.01m, South Yorkshire GBP 1.05m, and HSE EUR 3m), followed by Whzan, Inhealthcare and Docobo. Calmedica leads in France (AP-HP up to EUR 2.27m), and Cambio and Cuviva in Sweden. They win ICB and regional contracts, often through TECS2. They offer device supply and logistics, clinical monitoring and wearables (PF04, PF05, N522), none of which we have. Sources: [1](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/39dc6b3f-5320-4b0a-9705-3a7cf94f4880) [2](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/8d91a7af-3fe8-48eb-b92a-eb0a811e9019) [3](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/190143-2025) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/374454-2025/html) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/270851-2023/xml)
- **Scheduling (14).** Infix holds NHS Scotland's national theatre scheduling contract (GBP 6.3m). Trisoft sells theatre management with pre-assessment to ULHT, QEH King's Lynn and Salisbury. sqior leads German OR coordination (9 wins found, Heidelberg EUR 694,980). CIRUS (Osakidetza) and G.I.S.O. (Italian ASLs) hold regional renewals. They win national buys and repeated direct awards. They offer theatre lists, utilisation analytics and day-of-surgery flow (SW03, SW04, N226); Trisoft also puts pre-assessment in the same product. Sources: [1](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/017154-2024) [2](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/046773-2025) [3](https://www.salisbury.nhs.uk/about-us/freedom-of-information-foi/previous-foi-requests/foi_8903/) [4](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/346080-2025) [5](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/368907-2026/xml)
- **EPR vendors (13).** Dedalus has the most wins found (16: German KHZG portals, an Italian OR management system, Aragón's surgical process system). Epic MyChart runs GSTT's early screening tool and Northern Ireland's encompass portal; Altera Sunrise holds pre-op pro-formas inside the EPR at Dudley (contract ends about Dec 2026) and WWL, and System C Careflow does pre-op at Mersey and West Lancashire, where the cost cannot be split out; nexuzhealth wins whole Belgian EPRs with a patient portal (EUR 8.7m to 10m). They win the EPR contract and bundle pre-op into it. They offer one login, no integration project and native write-back; an EPR replacement is usually what triggers a stand-alone pre-op buy. Sources: [1](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/52876-2025/html) [2](https://healthinnovationnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/HIN-Evaluation-of-the-Digital-Early-Screening-Tool-on-the-GSTT-Perioperative-Pathway-Final-May-2026.pdf) [3](https://dhcni.hscni.net/digital-portfolio/encompass/) [4](https://www.dgft.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/FOI-072025-0001781.pdf) [5](https://www.merseywestlancs.nhs.uk//resources/download/sthk-68e764798fa590.26725952) [6](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/416167-2026) [7](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/477455-2025)

## 10. Pricing, revenue and the first sale

Added 2026-10-23. The prices and contract values below come from the sources linked. The totals, per-year conversions, revenue scenarios and cost figures are **our own arithmetic and assumptions**, marked as such.

### 10.1 What "one trust" means

Every value in this report is **per NHS trust** (in Scotland and Wales, per health board). The trust is the legal buyer. It often runs several hospitals and signs one contract that covers all its hospitals and pre-op clinics. The Welsh national buy covers every health board.

The price still scales with the trust's size, because suppliers price by volume, team or site:
- Open Medical Pathpoint ePOA: from £48,500 a year for one pre-op team, and from £74,500 a year for two or more teams. [1](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/706548/106177073699977-pricing-document-2026-01-29-0909.pdf)
- Ultramed MyPreOp and VitalHub Synopsis: per submission, so bigger trusts pay more. [2](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-pricing-document-2026-01-15-1455.pdf) [3](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/721733/214669371000433-pricing-document-2026-01-29-1809.pdf)
- Buddy Healthcare: £200 a month for each extra site. [4](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/719733/687667345372394-pricing-document-2026-01-07-1429.pdf)

Preopsis already models this: one trust, many hospitals, one tenancy.

**Typical range: about £50k to £92k a year per trust, with contracts of 1 to 3 years and many renewed every year.**

Implied volume (our arithmetic): at Ultramed's published £2.80–£5.00 per submission, UH Dorset's £92,160 a year matches roughly 18,000–33,000 pre-op submissions a year. At £2 per submission, a trust of about 20,000 submissions would pay about £40k a year.

Most incumbents include demographic lookup and document return in the price. **A cheaper bid without integration is not a like-for-like offer.**

This table is the short list. Section 10.7 has the full published pricing for every supplier found, including day rates, SMS charges, implementation fees, integration add-ons and minimum volumes. Section 10.8 lists every contract value found per supplier, 10.9 every tender with a stated value, and 10.10 every finding that mentions a price or cost.

**Our arithmetic:**
- Named English renewals plus possibly lapsed contracts: about **£470k a year**.
- Six greenfield trusts at benchmark: perhaps **£300–550k a year** (estimate).
- Wales: **~£830k a year** on its own.

### 10.5 Revenue needed for £1M a year profit (scenario, our assumptions)

**Assumption, not sourced:** running costs for a one-developer company that can bid are about £150–250k a year. That covers ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus, a yearly pen test, a contracted Clinical Safety Officer, insurance, accounting, and paid implementation and support help. £1M profit therefore needs **about £1.2M revenue a year**.

| Price per trust per year | Trusts needed for ~£1.2M |
|---|---|
| £40k (undercut everyone) | ~30 |
| £50k | ~24 |
| £65k (market median) | ~18 |
| £80k | ~15 |
| £100k (pre-op plus a consent or waiting-well bundle) | ~12 |

What the evidence implies:
- **Do not compete on price alone.** Price is about 25% of the score in the one open English pre-op tender (Royal Surrey: demos 25%, technical 25%, price 25%, requirement compliance 15%, social value 10%) [link](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/073826-2026). At £40k, 30 trusts are needed, against about 8 English trusts with a visible paid pre-op contract plus a handful of greenfield and lapsed ones. Price near the market rate (£60–75k) and win on triage, NHS App access and the demo.
- **Wales is the shortcut, but financial standing is a barrier.** Buyers test turnover and solvency: NHS Golden Jubilee required turnover of at least twice the contract value [link](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959), and AZORG required an Altman Z-score above 1.5 [link](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/702720-2026). A new solo company is unlikely to pass this for a £5m contract. The realistic route is to bid as a subcontractor or partner to a larger prime or a reseller (Softcat already resells Ultramed).
- **Bundles mean fewer trusts.** Consent sells at £45–100k a year per trust (Concentric, EIDO), and PROMs next to pre-op. Pre-op plus one partnered module at ~£100k means about 12 trusts.
- **Timing.** The renewal windows run from Mar 2027 to Mar 2028, and CDHS 2.0 goes live around Oct 2027 [link](https://www.publictechnology.net/?p=13604). Reaching 12–18 trusts is realistically a **3–4 year path** (our estimate).
- **The bottleneck is delivery, not the market.** Implementation, training and support appear in 115 tenders (section 3c), and each trust needs its own integration. One developer can build the product but cannot onboard and support 12–20 trusts alone. To keep margin high:
  - contract the Clinical Safety Officer;
  - sell through a framework or a reseller;
  - hire one implementation and support person after about 4–5 trusts;
  - standardise the integration pack.

### 10.6 Mandatory before the first hospital

Detail and sources for every item are in section 5.

**A. Hard gates (no real patient data without these).**

| # | Item | Why | Our state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DCB0129 clinical safety case, hazard log, named Clinical Safety Officer (a registered clinician; can be contracted) | Legal information standard; the trust does DCB0160 | Missing (planned C10) |
| 2 | DTAC v2.0 passed | NHS England baseline, mandatory from 6 Apr 2026; pass/fail parts are items 3–6 | Missing (no plan) |
| 3 | DSPT 'Standards Met', ICO registration, product DPIA, data processing agreement | DTAC C2 | Partial (planned C10) |
| 4 | Cyber Essentials and an independent pen test within 12 months (or sign the NHS Cyber Security Charter) | DTAC C3 | Missing (planned C10) |
| 5 | NHS Number validated against PDS or local records; documented open APIs | DTAC C4 | Partial (Modulus 11 check only) |
| 6 | Patient sign-in through NHS login, or one that meets DAPB3051 | DTAC C4; whether magic link + date of birth meets DAPB3051 needs checking | Missing (no plan) |
| 7 | Medical-device decision: register (UKCA Class I or higher) before selling auto-triage, or launch without it | MHRA guidance; DTAC C1 | Missing (no plan) |
| 8 | WCAG 2.2 AA audit and published accessibility statement | Public-sector accessibility regulations; DTAC D1 | Partial (no audit) |
| 9 | UK hosting | NHS off-shoring guidance | Done (AWS London) |

Plan C10 covers items 1, 3 and 4 (plus backups). **Items 2 and 5–8 are in no plan today.** The repo rule that no real patient data enters the system before C10 matches this list.

**B. Commercial must-haves.** A limited company with insurance (amounts are buyer-specific; NHS Golden Jubilee asked for £5m employer's liability and £2m professional indemnity [link](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959)), a price list, a support and SLA offer, and a contract route the trust can sign.

**C. Needed to win (not legally required).**
- **PAS/EPR integration** (demographics in, document back): every incumbent includes it (section 1, item 2).
- **A buying route:** G-Cloud or CDHS, or a reseller (section 1, item 3).
- **ISO 27001:** a tender filter, and the longest item to get.
- **One reference site:** a pilot or co-development deal is the cheapest first sale. Somerset ran a 'Peri-Operative Digital Solution Co-Development Opportunity' [link](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/031748-2024); the greenfield trusts in 10.4 fit best.

**Suggested order for a single developer** (our recommendation):
1. Start ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials, which are slow to certify, together with the DCB0129 work in C10 and a contracted Clinical Safety Officer.
2. Decide the device question before building C6.
3. Build the PAS integration pack and NHS login.
4. Run the pen test and the accessibility audit.
5. Complete DTAC.
6. Pilot at one greenfield trust.
7. List on G-Cloud and prepare for CDHS 2.0 (notice expected early 2027).
