- NHS Commercial Solutions' Patient Healthcare Communications and Related IT Services framework (£1.4bn, 2 Dec 2025-1 Dec 2033) has 13 lots, including Patient Messaging, App Development, Streamlined Patient Pathways/flow and AI-enabled Digital Care. It is a likely 'NHS framework' route for portal procurements such as ULHT's. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4b01b246-d069-49ec-ab9a-d2be725791e1)
- The All Wales PROMs Solution Framework (NWSSP, est. £11.9m, 3+1 years from Nov 2023) has five suppliers and lets health boards call off by mini-competition. The first call-off went to Promptly Health for four UHBs, with later onboardings (Velindre). [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/11/07/all-wales-proms-framework-agreement-worth-estimated-11m-awarded-to-five-suppliers/)
- NHS England ran a DrDoctor 'Clinical smart forms pilot: secondary care outpatient recovery & transformation' (£348,000, Feb 2023-Feb 2026), with a £75,000 SMS consumables variation in 2025. This shows national interest in digital clinical questionnaires. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7dd0e720-dcc8-40c4-b079-d72c8560032a)
- NHS England bought 'Clinical Smart Forms' from DrDoctor: £75,000, 2025-07-28 to 2026-02-13, awarded 2025-08-07. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/1361d99a-7b9e-49d5-a2f3-ce5304b274ea)
- West Hertfordshire Hospitals bought a 'Zesty Form Builder' (digital forms and questionnaires) for £100,000, 2024-03-31 to 2027-03-30, as a framework call-off. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/2ec6666c-bb54-4957-aeef-1ac9b334fb2a)
- Princess Alexandra Hospital switched portal suppliers from DrDoctor (G-Cloud 11, £60k, 2023–24) to Zesty. It also bought a separate CRIS-to-Zesty integration licence (£30.9k, 2025–26), so integration is costed separately from the portal licence. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/3091975c-443b-482a-99c9-91e554041c13)
- The joint Bradford/Airedale/Calderdale & Huddersfield PEP + hybrid mail procurement (BTH25-103, est. GBP 10.179m, 1 Mar 2026-28 Feb 2030 + 12 months) required native Oracle (Cerner) EPR integration, digital forms, waiting list validation, Wayfinder and NHS App alignment. It was awarded to Zesty, Xerox and Oracle on 24 Dec 2025, then terminated on 27 Jan 2026 with all contracts unsigned. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007304-2026)
- After the termination, Bradford placed a 12-month call-off (1 Mar 2026-28 Feb 2027, GBP 513k) for digital and hybrid mail patient letters with the incumbent DrDoctor. This points to a likely re-procurement window before Feb 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/d3d2477b-a5ec-423e-bef9-c7444e14cd14)
- Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS FT's PEP prior information notice (budget GBP 800k) asks for custom questionnaires and forms linked to the patient record, EPR booking integration, two-way messaging, proxy access, NHS App and Wayfinder. All patient data must be held in the EPR, and the solution must already be live at an NHS trust. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2025/01/06/hampshire-and-isle-of-wight-healthcare-nhs-plans-patient-engagement-portal-procurement/)
- ROH awarded a 10-year EPR (InterSystems, GBP 13.1m, Feb 2026 to Feb 2036) at about the time its 2-year DrDoctor engagement contract ended (Mar 2026). Pre-op and patient engagement tools may be re-procured around the new EPR. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/eb21056c-6ba3-4bb5-96b6-dcb409cb1f5f)
- HPFT FOI (Nov 2025): hybrid mail is via Cisco (formerly Healthcare Communications), first procured on G-Cloud 12. The current agreement runs 01/07/2025 to 30/06/2026 with two optional extensions. 70,940 hybrid letters a year. Zero letters via the NHS App because the trust had no PEP live on it. [source](https://www.hpft.nhs.uk/media/gsxolsed/2025-11-05-5877-disclosure-log-response.pdf)
- Bradford Teaching Hospitals awarded DrDoctor 'Patient Letters (Digital and Hybrid mail)' at GBP 513,151.95 in Aug 2026. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/d3d2477b-a5ec-423e-bef9-c7444e14cd14)
- NHS England awarded DrDoctor a 'Clinical Smart Forms' contract (GBP 75,000, Jun 2026). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/1361d99a-7b9e-49d5-a2f3-ce5304b274ea)
- The Institute of Oncology Ljubljana awarded an open tender for the development, implementation and 7-year maintenance of an Onkološki kirurški modul (oncology surgical module) to FIDURO d.o.o. for EUR 935,188.56 (90 months). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/249188-2026)
- Contracts Finder notice b62c55b2 (DrDoctor patient portal, GBP 865,000, 27 Oct 2023 to 26 Oct 2028) belongs to Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust. The portal lets patients view records and results, update appointments and request changes to planned surgery dates. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/b62c55b2-5418-4845-9233-ad9840d42162)
- Hull University Teaching Hospitals awarded a DrDoctor patient engagement platform via G-Cloud 13 (RM1557.13), GBP 101,016, 30 Mar 2024 to 29 Mar 2025. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7bec8dbf-2dec-4213-b88c-bed546fcaeda)
- Gateshead Health published a separate GBP 37,000 Cancer Prehabilitation Programme (a structured 12-week pathway for 120 patients over 12 months) on 23 Jan 2026, with no supplier shown on the public page. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-060da0)
- In a feasibility study of Surgery Hero at the Northern Gynaecological Oncology Centre, Gateshead (Apr to May 2024), 15 of 29 eligible patients activated, with 93% participation and 4.5/5 satisfaction. The main barrier was a median of 20 days from consent to surgery. Licences cost GBP 150 + VAT each. [source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12441255/)
- Buyer pattern: several NHS digital prehab buys are small, 12-month, below-threshold direct awards with no competition (West Herts GBP 51k, Gateshead GBP 19k), so renewals come round each year without a tender. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/083730-2025)
- University Hospitals Plymouth contracted QuestPrehab for a year-long digital prehab trial for liver-transplant waiting-list patients (Devon, Cornwall, Somerset). [source](https://htn.co.uk/2024/07/17/telehealth-provider-chosen-for-digital-prehab-trial-in-devon-cornwall-and-somerset/)
- Devon's digital waiting-list validation programme (Netcall, linked to the NHS App, for the Devon Referral Support Service covering Torbay and Royal Devon) ran 2023-09-13 to 2026-09-12, GBP 132,195. Its term has just ended, so a re-procurement or extension in Devon is likely now or imminent. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c)
- Oct 2023 Induction RNS: Royal Free London (GBP 346k) and South West London ICB (GBP 577k) contracts included Form Builder for waitlist validation. Trusts buy questionnaire tooling under the waiting-list validation banner. [source](https://www.inductionhealthcare.com/regulatory-news/update-on-nhs-national-portals-contracts)
- Trusts typically buy patient-questionnaire and validation software as small direct call-offs (G-Cloud, NHS SBS, NHS Commercial Solutions, COCH F075) of GBP 50k-300k, often published on Contracts Finder months after award with no public specification. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/2ec6666c-bb54-4957-aeef-1ac9b334fb2a)
- Princess Alexandra Hospital contracted the Zesty patient engagement portal for GBP 155,000 via an NHS SBS framework call-off, to end of March 2027. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/07/14/princess-alexandra-hospital-contracts-patient-engagement-portal/)
- TRUST MAP – Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust: Ultramed is the pre-op supplier. Evidence: a Contracts Finder award. First seen: a VitalHub 'Digital Pre Op Solution' ran Feb–Oct 2024 (GBP 81k). Ultramed was then direct-awarded 2024-11-01 to 2027-10-31 (GBP 240k, about GBP 80k/yr, framework call-off through Atamis). The trust's spend files are blocked by Cloudflare, so payments could not be checked. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- TRUST MAP – Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn NHS FT: Ultramed Ultraprep licences (Contracts Finder), GBP 51,300 for 2024-04-01 to 2025-03-31, framework call-off. No later renewal notice was found. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/e3b61de0-a98d-42a1-a6b9-d5c86600a54e)
- TRUST MAP – North West Anglia NHS FT: Ultramed Ultraprep (digital POA) bought through Softcat as a direct award on Digital Workplace Solutions 2. GBP 222,720 for 2026-06-01 to 2029-05-31, covering implementation, demographic and document-upload integration, and patient and staff support. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- TRUST MAP – University Hospitals Dorset NHS FT: Ultramed MyPreOp. A 12-month renewal bought through Softcat on a framework, GBP 92,160 for 2026-04-01 to 2027-03-31. Because it is a renewal, use started earlier, but the first date was not found. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2d78f3b3-5b19-4be3-86cf-3700525e3272)
- TRUST MAP – George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust: an Ultramed Limited payment of GBP 40,200 (cost centre Surgery Services, Computer Software), dated 01/07/24, in the trust's over-GBP 25k file. No Contracts Finder notice was found, so this was probably a below-threshold or framework buy. Isla's website also lists George Eliot (use not stated). [source](https://www.geh.nhs.uk/download_file/1627/295)
- TRUST MAP – Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust: uses MyPreOp per the Ultramed case study (270 more clinic slots a month; 34% more capacity). No payment to Ultramed over GBP 25k appears in RWT spend files for Apr 2025–Sep 2026. The trust paid Zesty Ltd GBP 114,000 (IT, Sep 2025) for its portal. [source](https://ultramed.co/case-study-the-royal-wolverhampton)
- TRUST MAP – London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust: uses MyPreOp per an Ultramed case study (40% more clinical capacity within a year; 10,000+ patients). Ultramed's home page also cites Walsall Healthcare (lead nurse, pre-assessment) and Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital. No Contracts Finder notices exist for any of the three. [source](https://ultramed.co/case-studies)
- TRUST MAP – Somerset NHS FT: Open Medical Pathpoint ePOA. The call-off runs 2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31 at GBP 106,850, about GBP 53k/yr. An earlier case study reports 65.43% same-day responses and 67% completion. Its new EHR rollout is planned for 2028. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/1c16e332-f07c-4e99-b288-ff1e68cf56e1)
- TRUST MAP – Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust: Open Medical Pathpoint ePOA, bought yearly on the CDHS for the Integrated Health Economy framework (GBP 74k in 2025/26; GBP 76k in 2026/27). Its EPR is Alex Health (Cerner, live Nov 2024), which had no digital POA function. Pathpoint is fed by a waiting-list export (ETL), not a direct integration. [source](https://www.openmedical.co.uk/blog/open-medical-pathpoint-epoa-supporting-elective-recovery-at-princess-alexandra-hospital-nhs-trust-with-implementation-of-digital-pre-operative-assessment-platform)
- TRUST MAP – West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust: Open Medical Pathpoint SurgiCare for POA since Oct 2020, used across linked POA departments with escalation to anaesthetists. Its EPR/PAS is Oracle Cerner Millennium. Its portal and waiting-list validation run on Induction Zesty (G-Cloud 13 call-off, GBP 100k, 2024-27). [source](https://www.openmedical.co.uk/case-studies/harnessing-digital-technology-to-manage-elective-surgical-backlog)
- TRUST MAP – Northumbria Healthcare NHS FT: VitalHub 'Pre Assessment Software' (product not named), GBP 123,985.08 for 2025-07-06 to 2027-07-05, framework call-off with no extension. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ecfccd32-f3aa-4601-b26f-c29dc6ed5ed8)
- TRUST MAP – Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS FT: Isla Health Digital Health Questionnaires for pre-op triage. Green-light patients skip face-to-face POA. Reported results: 57% fewer on-the-day theatre cancellations, 135+ clinical hours recovered and GBP 731,852 saved. No tender or award notice was found. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/03/10/scaling-clinical-excellence-and-efficiency-lessons-from-chelsea-and-westminster-nhs-foundation-trust/)
- TRUST MAP – Hull University Teaching Hospitals (and the Humber and North Yorkshire partners York and Scarborough, Harrogate and NLaG): a digital pre-assessment pathway on Patients Know Best questionnaires (HTN 2023). The PKB portal was re-awarded 2025-03-31 to 2027-03-30, GBP 669,927, as a direct award under NHS SBS TECS 2. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/05/05/deep-dive-coverage-benefits-and-research-on-patient-portals/)
- POSSIBLE GREENFIELD (with caveats) – In the over-GBP 25k spend files checked (data.gov.uk links, roughly 2023–2026), no payment to any pre-op supplier was found for: Portsmouth Hospitals UHT (only Concentric consent through Softcat and a Healthcare Communications portal), Dudley Group (PKB GBP 160k Jul 2026; Healthcare Communications), Isle of Wight (Healthcare Communications), Milton Keynes UH (Zesty portal only), East Sussex Healthcare (PKB portal, Netcall, Accurx) and United Lincolnshire (Eido, Open Medical MSK, Netcall). Payments under GBP 25k or through resellers would not show, and vendor websites (e.g. Isla) list some of these trusts. [source](https://www.mkuh.nhs.uk/document/mkh_spend_01-feb-2024_to_29-feb-2024)
- PRICE BENCHMARKS – Annual software cost for digital POA in English acute trusts runs about GBP 51k–92k: QEH Ultraprep GBP 51.3k, Somerset Pathpoint about GBP 53k/yr, Northumbria VitalHub about GBP 62k/yr, PAHT Pathpoint GBP 74–76k, NWAFT Ultraprep about GBP 74k/yr, Worcestershire Ultramed about GBP 80k/yr, UHD MyPreOp GBP 92k. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/31980e5b-7425-4133-8d72-135bfe8294c1)
- Resah's 2025 innovation catalogue (2024-R063, 17 lots) awarded on 2025-04-28. Consent management went to DrData, PROMs to SKEZI and PREMs to BETTER WORLD, each at EUR 10M maximum. The operating-theatre flow and coordination lot (010) closed without a winner. French hospitals can buy these without their own tender. [source](https://boamp-datadila.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/boamp/records?where=idweb%3D%2225-68840%22)
- Resah 2026-R035 is a single-supplier, end-to-end patient-pathway framework with AI modules: EUR 80M estimated, EUR 250M maximum, up to 73 months from 2026-12-01. Resah justified the long term because the AI modules may not be on the market at notification. [source](https://boamp-datadila.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/boamp/records?where=idweb%3D%2226-63480%22)
- UniHA's SAD M_3399 (EUR 30M estimated, open until June 2031) is the open route for new digital care-pathway vendors to get referenced with UniHA. Members run specific contracts and invite every admitted operator. Seven operators were admitted by March 2026. [source](https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr/index.php?page=Entreprise.EntrepriseDownloadReglement&id=Mjc5MzYzMw==&orgAcronyme=x7c)
- CAIH carries a digital medical consent offer: CHU Toulouse bought 'CAIH Consentement Médical' from Docaposte for EUR 470,000 (2025). The CAIH contracts visible in DECP are otherwise mostly infrastructure. [source](https://tabular-api.data.gouv.fr/api/resources/22847056-61df-452d-837d-8b8ceadbfc52/data/?objet__contains=CAIH)
- French pre-admission and follow-up incumbents are often renewed by negotiated award without competition, e.g. CHU Limoges–Exolis ENGAGE (pre-admission module) and AP-HP–Calmedica Memoquest (EUR 2.27M). Market entry depends on catalogue referencing or the incumbent's renewal date. [source](https://tabular-api.data.gouv.fr/api/resources/22847056-61df-452d-837d-8b8ceadbfc52/data/?titulaire_nom__contains=EXOLIS)
- ERAS programmes are a growing purchase category in Italy: ASST Valcamonica EUR 635,800 (2026), Niguarda EUR 210,000 (2025), AO Brotzu EUR 180,000, FTGM EUR 120,000 for 36-month ERAS® certification, AUSL Romagna ERAS audit via Medtronic EIAS, and ULSS 2 DREAM ERAS teleconsultation (B. Braun). [source](https://dati.anticorruzione.it/opendata/download/dataset/cig/filesystem/20261001-cig_csv.zip)
- Niguarda (Milan) is extending its Smart Data Platform/INVITA360 for a prericovero (pre-admission) project, worth EUR 323,000 (2026-08). This is the clearest Italian digital pre-op signal found. [source](https://dati.anticorruzione.it/opendata/download/dataset/cig/filesystem/20260901-cig_csv.zip)
- The IOV Padova 'preospedalizzazione' contract (TED 689852-2023, EUR 960,000) is outsourced front- and back-office staff, not software, so it was excluded. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/689852-2023/xml)
- The HSE Health App now shows hospital appointments shared by 36 public hospitals, 23 community services and two surgical hubs (Cork and Swords). It also shows inpatient/day-case waiting lists with priority status (no wait time), discharge summaries and GP referrals. 'Coming soon' items include checking wait times and 'reading information before and after appointments'. The app does not mention pre-op questionnaires. [source](https://www2.hse.ie/health-app/about-your-hse-health-app/)
- HSE purchase orders over EUR 20k for Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 show no line for Ultramed, Oneview, Patients Know Best, EIDO, Concentric, DrDoctor, Netcall, Zesty or Marino. Digital-health engagement lines that do appear: myPatientSpace, Open Medical (OLOL, Cavan), Swiftqueue, patientMpower, Doccla, Dendrite, Qualtrics, DocuSign (EUR 80,678 ICT subscription), System C/Careflow (about EUR 852k once-off licences Q4 2025), Cerner, Dedalus, InterSystems, Clanwilliam. The file does not name the hospital. [source](https://about.hse.ie/publications/payments-to-suppliers-purchase-orders-over-20000-q4-2025)
- The HSE Q1 2026 purchase-order file (over EUR 20k) is published as CSV on about.hse.ie. Earlier quarters (2024–Q3 2025) could not be found at the same URL pattern. [source](https://about.hse.ie/publications/payments-to-suppliers-purchase-orders-over-20000-q1-2026)
- St Vincent's University Hospital Q1 2026 payments over EUR 20k list iMDsoft (perioperative/critical care clinical information system vendor) and Trend Care Systems, among others. No pre-op, consent or PROMs vendor appears. [source](https://www.stvincents.ie/app/uploads/2026/04/SVUH-Q1-2026-Payments-over-E20k.pdf)
- Mater Misericordiae University Hospital ran a 2023 tender to replace its PatientCentre PAS/EPR but could not award it for budget reasons. In Dec 2024 it direct-awarded Dedalus EUR 1.4m over 4 years to move PatientCentre to the cloud; any replacement will need a full tender. The Mater has no modern EPR to embed pre-op functions, so a standalone pre-op tool would be needed. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/789956-2024)
- Royal Victoria Eye & Ear Hospital VEAT (Aug 2024): its bespoke CAPAS PAS reached end of life 10 years earlier and is top of the risk register. It has waited for the HSE iPMS since 2017, and PFH got EUR 324,000 for support and migration. This shows how slowly Irish voluntary hospitals replace core systems. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/520980-2024)
- HSE National Shared Care Record (HSE 21246): competitive dialogue awarded to Ernst and Young (as named on TED) at EUR 81.7m for 20 years (contract 18 Mar 2025). It aggregates hospital, GP and community records for clinicians and for patients at the point of care and self-care, making it a possible patient-facing channel alongside the HSE Health App. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/387406-2025)
- HSE Critical Care Clinical Information System awarded to Uniphar Medtech Ltd t/a Cardiac Services, EUR 7.08m (contract 20 Feb 2025, 4 tenders). The HSE reserved the right to reuse the outcome across HSE and HSE-funded hospitals. National framework-style reuse is a common HSE buying pattern. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/194830-2025)
- St Vincent's University Hospital published a preliminary market consultation (Sep/Oct 2026, est. EUR 300k) for moving from paper-based to electronic referrals with configurable workflows for National Cancer Care Pathways. Pathway-digitisation PMCs are how SVUH tests the market before tendering. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/681141-2026)
- The Gerechtshof Arnhem-Leeuwarden (ECLI:NL:GHARL:2026:2351, reported 22 April 2026) overturned ChipSoft's injunction and lifted the EUR 100,000/day penalty. UMCG, OZG and Treant need not re-tender the shared Epic EPD, because the 2015 tender included the regional option. Treant is shown as a NovaCair E-POS logo customer, so its pre-op tooling may move with the Epic switch. [source](https://www.dutchitchannel.nl/news/730331/chipsoft-verliest-hoger-beroep-over-regionaal-pati%C3%ABntendossier)
- AZ Jan Palfijn Gent awarded a single-supplier framework for an integrated EPD to ChipSoft ZIS B.V., award value EUR 117,626,479.61, concluded 2026-07-24, 10 years per the PIN. Pre-op screening there will default to HiX. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/646663-2026)
- QEH King's Lynn bought Ultraprep licences each year with falling spend (2022/23 £137,854.20; 2023/24 £74,856.96; 2024/25 £51,300). No 2025/26 or 2026/27 notice exists on Contracts Finder, so the account may have lapsed or be running on unpublished renewals, and it is worth approaching. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2a16f909-6217-466a-8958-111cacff13b8)
- ESNEFT bought 'Digitisation of Pre-Operative Assessment' (CA7369) via Softcat for £276,000: 3 years from 2020-09-01 with an option of 24 more months (maximum about 2025-09-01). No successor notice was found on Contracts Finder, so this is another possibly lapsed or unpublished pre-op renewal. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/33e19a48-8a0e-4f96-abaf-c7db9f244637)
- Chesterfield (DSFS) held MyPreOp software from 2020-02-01 to 2024-01-31 (£129,199), and Dorset County Hospital held UltraPrep/MyPreOP licences from 2022-03-30 to 2024-03-29 (£76,800). Neither has a published successor on Contracts Finder, so both are possible renewal or replacement targets. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/d81390f5-8fdf-4571-b7b8-2f865a6eedb4)
- ULHT turned a one-year single-tender Eido consent-leaflet licence (2025/26, £40,701.80) into a 3-year framework call-off (2026-07-31 to 2029-07-30, up to £129,130.27). The notice was published 2026-10-22, nearly 3 months after the term started. This is a pattern of 1-year pilots converting to 3-year terms. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/df666f8b-808a-4f66-9e88-472dc2ba2ecb)
- The NHS Devon waiting-list validation contract with Netcall (£132,195, required NHS App linkage) expired on 2026-09-12. No re-procurement or extension notice is on Contracts Finder, so this is a live opening. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/a8ae9f2f-5542-4bab-8cde-23d0a176b17c)
- The All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, £11.9m awarded) was set up for '3 years with an option to extend for a year' (48 months) from 13 Oct 2023. Its initial term ended about Oct 2026 and the maximum runs to about Oct 2027, so an all-Wales PROMs re-procurement is likely during 2027. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/031093-2022)
- The NHS England Outcomes and Registries transition contract with NEC (£4.16m) ends 2027-09-30, so the national PROMs/registries platform replacement must be in market by about Q1 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9)
- ULS Coimbra (Portugal) renewed UpHill Route 'Percurso Clínicos Integrados Peri-Operatório' maintenance and licensing by direct award: EUR 139,650 for 1096 days from 2025-11-03, so it ends about 2028-11-03 (estimated). Portuguese perioperative-pathway buyers renew incumbents by direct award on 3-year cycles. [source](https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=11991481)
- Procurement Act UK7 'contract details' notices on Find a Tender now carry explicit contract dates and extension headroom for small below-threshold renewals: Gateshead Surgery Hero £19k, NNUH PROMs £15.4k, CoCH Eido with extension to 2030-05-13. FTS has become the main source for small renewals since Feb 2025. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/058752-2026)
- Other perioperative-adjacent contracts found while dating records (not in the existing set): Walton Centre DrDoctor platform 2024-03-31 to 2026-03-30 (£148,425); Newcastle radiology DrDoctor portal from 2024-12-31 (£148,073); WSFT Synertec patient communication 2025-07-01 to 2026-10-31 (£700,000). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/search_notices/json)
- DHCW's all-Wales Pre-Operative Digital System (est. £5m excl. VAT, Jan 2027 to Dec 2032 plus 2 years) had its tender notice estimated for 1 May 2026, but by 22 Oct 2026 the FTS procurement record still held only the UK2 engagement notice. The tender is late and could appear at any time. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-06667b)
- The NI Elective Care Framework (May 2024) plans single regional waiting lists once encompass is fully live. It funded mega clinics including 2,100 pre-operative patients to cut DNA and CNA rates, asks Trusts to validate waiting lists regularly by contacting patients (Action 10), and estimates about £500k for a waiting-well policy. [source](https://www.health-ni.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/health/Elective%20Care%20Framework%20-%20May%202024.pdf)
- Ultramed is winning share. Worcestershire Acute replaced VitalHub Synopsis (£81k bridging term to Oct 2024) with Ultramed (£240k, Nov 2024 to Oct 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/3e45d535-f2a1-4b00-a86c-5535f81031a9)
- Digital Health & Care Wales plans an all-Wales pre-op digital system (£5m, 2027 to 2032, extendable to 2034). As of Oct 2026 only the PME (Mar 2026) has been published. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021393-2026)
- Belgium's AZORG has a live tender for a digital pre-op screening system (deadline 10 Nov 2026, 48 months), weighted 50% price, 30% technical/IT and 20% quality including a demo. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/702720-2026/xml)
- Digital consent is a fast-growing adjacent category. Concentric and EIDO won at least 7 NHS awards between 2024 and 2026 (£105k to £300k each), and South Tees has an open tender for Digital Consent and Shared Decision Making (£135k, starting Jan 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Published prices give pricing benchmarks: Ultraprep £2.50 to £5.00 per submission; Synopsis £2.90 to £3.50 per unit; Pathpoint ePOA £48,500 per instance a year; AireFrame £2,500 per licence a year; Remcare £3 to £10 per user a year. [source](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/702415/799143724896306-pricing-document-2026-01-15-1455.pdf)
- Buyer pattern: the NHS Scotland national theatre scheduling ITT asked bidders to evidence Cyber Essentials, ISO 9001, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018 and the UK Government 14 Cloud Security Principles, scored functional 40, non-functional 30 and price 30. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-03b258)
- Market scale signal: UK Halle processed about 116,000 consent forms per year through the E-ConsentPro base module before digitising. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/851883-2025/xml)
- Wales plans a single national pre-op system (DHCW, GBP 5m ex VAT, 2027-2032 plus extensions to 2034). The planned tender date of 1 May 2026 passed with no tender notice found on Sell2Wales by 22 Oct 2026, so the procurement looks delayed but live. [source](https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=MAR596518)
- Belfast HSC Trust board paper P74-2025: pre-op assessment has historically been under-funded and resources are inadequate. The executive team approved a business case on 2 Dec 2024 for a fully functional adult pre-operative assessment service (Option 2, phased), with a funding request of GBP 1,688,649, to cut on-the-day cancellations and raise day-of-surgery admission. The paper names no software procurement. [source](https://belfasttrust.hscni.net/download/730/09-january-2025/21913/p74-2025-bhsct-meeting-template-adult-pre-operative-assessment-services-bhsct-excludes-mph-and-paediatric-pre-assessment.pdf)
- The Golden Jubilee perioperative app tender shows what a Scottish buyer scores. It was 60% quality / 40% price, with pass/fail 'must haves' (HL7 v2.4 in and out, RBAC, encryption, MFA, audit logs, DPIA, UK GDPR, the 2018 accessibility regulations) and declarations on medical-device status. An on-site demo scored the ability to change pathway content locally, such as turning a smoking info page into a smoking/vaping questionnaire without supplier involvement. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT516959)
- Scotland's national Digital Front Door (MyCare.scot) is being built by NES with BJSS/CGI (GBP 27.85m). New national digital tenders, such as the Oct 2026 MSK PMC, now require compatibility with MyCare.scot. Scottish pre-op questionnaires will likely be expected to integrate with it. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=OCT566180)
- WLAP 2025: surgical hubs are being built in South Dublin (opening early 2025), North Dublin (Q4 2025), Galway (H1 2026), and Cork, Waterford and Limerick (phased 2026), with one under consideration in the North West. Once open they add 4,000 day cases, 5,800 minor procedures and 18,500 OPD appointments a year. [source](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/waiting-list-action-wlap-2025.pdf)
- Galway (Merlin Park) Surgical Hub construction contract awarded to John Sisk and Son, EUR 38.4m. The building has operating theatres, preparation, recovery and waiting areas, and targets day-case waiting lists in the West (Sláintecare Action Plan 2023). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/534590-2026)
- NTPF is setting up a EUR 700m, 48-month framework of private healthcare providers for adult and paediatric day case, inpatient and outpatient procedures (tenders closed 18 Sep 2026). This keeps outsourced elective surgery, and so pre-op assessment demand, flowing to private hospitals. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/551152-2026)
- Mater Misericordiae University Hospital tendered for a replacement patient management system in 2023 but could not award for budget reasons. In Dec 2024 it contracted Dedalus to move PatientCentre to the cloud (EUR 1.4m, 4 years) while it seeks funding to replace it. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/789956-2024)
- St James's Hospital is implementing an Oracle Cerner PAS, capacity management/patient flow and billing, with a consultancy tender (EUR 3m) in 2024 and again in 2026. The Rotunda and MN-CMS run Oracle Cerner Millennium, where hospitals want embedded SMART on FHIR apps. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/501868-2024)
- UMCNL consultation outcome: respondents see multichannel delivery, adaptive questionnaires, dashboards and EPR integration as standard. They expect PREMs and PROMs to be increasingly combined with other data, and recommend a roughly 4-year contract with licence plus usage pricing. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/414102/documenten/14156625/content)
- Amsterdam UMC used a VEAT to award a 3-year contract (EUR 266k/yr) for the ikHerstel perioperative recovery app without competition, citing unique evidence-based algorithms and RCT evidence. This is a precedent for direct awards to evidence-backed perioperative apps. [source](https://www.tenderned.nl/papi/tenderned-rs-tns/v2/publicaties/402893/documenten/13378635/content)
- In Belgium, HiX (ChipSoft) won the AZ Jan Palfijn Gent EPR framework (EUR 143.5M result value, 2026). ZAS also runs HiX and integrates via FHIR, so HiX integration matters in Flanders as well as the Netherlands. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/646663-2026)
- The Dutch Ministry of Health (VWS) is funding work to embed shared decision-making (samen beslissen) in medical specialist care. CQT groep won the training contract (EUR 577,605, 2025), part of the Uitkomstgerichte Zorg (outcome-based care) programme context. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/612505-2025)
- 2M-IT Oy awarded Satakunta's anaesthesia system to GE Healthcare Finland Oy (EUR 1,308,632, contract 2025-07-07): four years with an indefinite-extension option and an optional ICU module, after the first round closed with no winner (TED 237421-2025). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/521704-2025)
- France's RESAH launched a national single-supplier framework for an end-to-end patient-pathway platform with AI modules: EUR 80m estimated, EUR 250m maximum, up to 73 months from 2026-12-01. One winner will be able to supply all French public hospitals. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/442265-2026/html)
- RESAH's 2024-25 innovation framework already holds single-supplier lots for PROMs (SKEZI), PREMs (Better World) and consent (DrData), each capped at EUR 10m. The operating-block flow-coordination lot had 2 bids but no award, so it is a gap that could be relaunched. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/399745-2025/html)
- RESAH scores digital solutions on functional/technical quality including hosting (35 points), price (25), innovation (15), services and interfacing (15), means (5) and CSR (5). [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/399745-2025/html)
- The UniHA innovation SAD (EUR 30m, open to 2031) lets suppliers register at any time. UniHA can add categories (20 so far, none pre-op), and applications must be in French. [source](https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr/entreprise/consultation/2793633?orgAcronyme=x7c)
- Portuguese ULS hospitals often buy small (EUR 9k-40k) through Consulta Prévia with short bid windows (11-22 days) on Vortal, and several perioperative contracts are awarded on price alone. [source](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/cp_hora/2026/07/126/419965980.pdf)
- Madrid public hospitals pilot PROMs/PREMs, consent digitisation and AI surgical scheduling through contratos menores just under EUR 15,000, which are published only on the regional portal. [source](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/contrato/D540_8933)
- Spain's NextGenerationEU-funded Plan de Asistencia/Atención Digital Personalizada drives regional patient-facing platform tenders. Aragón's ADP platform went to T-Systems for EUR 1.3m, and its specification refers to 17 pilot projects due by 2026-06-30. [source](https://contrataciondelestado.es/wps/poc?uri=deeplink:detalle_licitacion&idEvl=YzaITRuazvBq1DdmE7eaXg%3D%3D)
- Italian regions also buy OR and surgical systems through Consip 'Sanità Digitale' frameworks (for example, the Marche regional operating-block system was awarded at quality 90 / price 10). The new Consip AQ ID 2837 (Data Governance & AI, EUR 662.4m, 4 lots) is a further framework that only admitted suppliers can use. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/421722-2024/html)
- Italian OR/surgical pathway tenders bundle pre-op anaesthesia assessment into large clinician-side systems (EUR 1.8m-5m) rather than buying patient-facing pre-op questionnaires separately. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/722510-2026/html)
- Polish operating-block software awards are price-only and won by the HIS incumbent (one bid at GCM Katowice), which limits openings for a foreign SaaS entrant. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/702142-2024/html)
- Portuguese hospitals are starting dedicated value-based-healthcare platform tenders (CROMs/PROMs/PREMs) weighted 70% on quality, e.g. ULS Gaia/Espinho at EUR 210k (2026). [source](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/cp_hora/2026/08/168/419971626.pdf)
- CHU Coimbra bought PROMs/PREMs, telemonitoring and OMOP project support from NTT Data Portugal by direct award (EUR 19,900, 2024), showing PROMs programmes run by integrators. [source](https://www.base.gov.pt/Base4/pt/detalhe/?type=contratos&id=10729497)
- In Germany and Belgium, pre-op (Prämedikation / pre-anaesthesia consultation) is often bought inside anaesthesia information systems (AIMS). HeCaPP made a pre-op consultation module a required option in a 10-year anaesthesia software contract (EUR 1.07M, ICARE). Albertinen Hamburg required the AIMS to cover the Prämedikation visit and send its summary to the KIS. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/1380-2026)
- Digital consent in Germany is concentrated with Thieme Compliance (E-ConsentPro). It won Aachen, Köln (EUR 883,780.91), Halle (EUR 338,287), the Albertinen group, Mittelrhein, Fürstenfeldbruck, Charité and Rhön. Halle alone processes about 116,000 consent forms a year. Buyers now ask for consent forms pre-filled from KIS or portal anamnesis data and an at-home workflow. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/851883-2025)
- In German OR coordination, sqior medical has won repeated direct awards on uniqueness grounds (MHH, Heidelberg EUR 694,980, Rostock, Erlangen, LMU, Bonn, Freiburg, Mannheim; Mainz planned). Bonn ran an EU-wide market sounding (PIN) first and then direct-awarded. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/300707-2026)
- ERAS software buying in the EU points to Encare. UK Münster's 2026 market consultation set minimum requirements (ERAS Society authorisation, 11 specialty programmes, a digital prehabilitation module, audit and benchmarking platform, EIAS data migration) that effectively describe the incumbent. Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana (2025, EUR 100k) said EIAS was the only system it knew. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/509259-2026)
- France's central purchasing body GIP RESAH holds single-supplier 5-year frameworks (up to EUR 10M each) for PROMs (SKEZI), PREMs (BETTER WORLD), consent (DrData) and telemedicine (ROFIM). Its operating-theatre flow/coordination lot was declared without award for insufficient competition. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/399745-2025)
- Region Hovedstaden (Denmark) puts its regional volume at about 600,000 surgical procedures a year (of about 2 million in Denmark). Its needs assessment for reducing postoperative complications asks for PRO data collection, multidisciplinary risk decision support, shared decision-making with the surgeon, and better pre-anaesthesia access to patient information. Innovation partnership(s) were planned for 2024. [source](https://eu.eu-supply.com/app/docmgmt/downloadPublicDocument.asp?FMT=5&AT=3&LID=451184&DVID=16034215)
- Belgian EPR replacements bundle perioperative and questionnaire features. HH Ziekenhuis Lier's EUR 8.69M, 120-month EPR (nexuzhealth) includes the anaesthesia nursing record, OR planning, and a patient portal for questionnaires with itsme authentication. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/416167-2026)
- Post-procedure remote monitoring is being bought through small direct awards in the Netherlands: Amsterdam UMC gave ikHerstel B.V. a 36-month award (estimated EUR 266,000 a year, about 750 users a month) for an app guiding physical recovery after procedures. [source](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/70081-2026)
- On Contracts Finder, digital pre-op assessment purchases are small call-offs or direct awards, typically £50k–£250k, made under frameworks rather than open tenders. Routes seen: G-Cloud 13/14, Digital Workplace Solutions 2, the LPP Clinical Digital Health Solutions (CDHS) framework, NOE Total Technology Solutions and NHS SBS. No open pre-op assessment competition was published on Contracts Finder between Oct 2023 and Oct 2026. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Worcestershire Acute switched pre-op supplier in 2024: a Vitalhub interim term (Feb–Oct 2024, £81k) was followed by a 3-year Ultramed contract (£240k, Nov 2024–Oct 2027). Incumbents can be displaced. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- NHS Commercial Solutions is setting up a £1.4bn Patient Healthcare Communications and Related IT Services framework (2025-12 to 2033-12, 13 lots, including Lot 11 Streamlined Patient Pathways/flow and Lot 12 AI-enabled Digital Care). It replaces the NHSE-endorsed framework and requires compliance with government open standards. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4b01b246-d069-49ec-ab9a-d2be725791e1)
- Digital consent is an active adjacent market on Contracts Finder (Eido, Concentric). South Tees has a live evaluation for a Digital Consent and Shared Decision Making solution (£135k, 3+1+1 years, start Jan 2027), so bundling consent or SDM with pre-op is a credible offer. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- Large EPR awards on Contracts Finder (e.g. Mid Yorkshire's £38.03m 10-year Nervecentre EPR via the LPP CDHS framework, Feb 2026) do not name perioperative or pre-op questionnaire scope in the public notice. EPR consolidation is still a risk to standalone pre-op tools. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/3310b148-e5ce-4725-85da-c93412854033)
- A theatre system replacement at Northumbria (replacing Nexus Sapphire, about 1,000+ users) asked bidders to cost a flexible licence model (concurrent, perpetual, subscription or enterprise) because user numbers may change. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/5c2dc86f-b71f-4768-a52f-4728e0bfb2b8)
- UK buying for digital consent is dominated by direct awards and framework call-offs (G-Cloud 13, OE Total Technology Solutions), usually with price as the only award criterion and one tender received. South Tees (Sept 2026) is the only open competitive tender found for consent plus SDM, and it scores on more than price. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/083956-2026)
- An impact assessment by Health Innovation Oxford and Thames Valley (funded by the HTA&A Fund via BOB ICB) found Concentric digital consent saved over 7 minutes per consent episode at OUH ophthalmology. It projected £5.64 saved per episode, about £167k over 3 years at around 825 episodes a month. [source](https://www.healthcare-management.uk/widespread-digitisation-consenting-process-bring-multiple-benefits)
- A peer-reviewed micro-costing study (Imperial) found a paper consent episode costs about £0.90 more than a digital one, and estimated an average saving of £201,590 per litigation claim prevented. [source](https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/entities/publication/3212282c-4402-4de4-843a-16f5962e5546)
- Medway NHS FT's FOI (Sept 2024) shows a typical trust: EIDO patient information leaflets in every department at £13,691.64 a year (renewal 12 Aug 2025), but no e-consent solution in any department, including surgery. That is a whitespace for digital consent. [source](https://www.medway.nhs.uk/uploads/2024/09/FOI-9056-Contracts-Procurement-September-2024.docx)
- NHS England's 2026/27 Referrals and Appointments fund (£15-20m, bids closed 31 May 2026) targets BaRS, e-RS, the NHS App/Wayfinder, PIFU and GIRFT pathway transformation. Trade-press coverage does not mention consent or pre-op; that funding route for consent rests only on a vendor's reading of offer 3a. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2026/05/15/up-to-20-million-national-funding-for-referrals-and-appointments-opens/)
- Policy direction toward EPR-native NHS App integration: NHSE capital funded a TPP direct award (£960k) for SystmOne-to-NHS App (Wayfinder) integration. A consultancy commentary claims NHSE has 'put on notice' standalone PEP suppliers (DrDoctor, PKB, Induction Zesty), citing about £11m a year in savings. That is commentary, not an NHSE document. [source](https://www.healthcare.digital/single-post/the-disintermediation-of-patient-portals-in-england-the-nhs-app-direct-epr-integrations-and-digita)
- University Hospitals of Leicester hired Apira (Jul-Oct 2026, £58.2k) to map every PEP and patient-facing system at UHL, run a gap analysis and gather requirements for new systems. This points to a UHL PEP procurement in 2027. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/571540ec-93ba-4400-9c67-c32b524ba8cd)
- Pre-op call-off values are small and renewed yearly or over 2–3 years: about £51k–£123k a year (PAHT Pathpoint £74–76k a year; UHD MyPreOp £92k a year; Northumbria VitalHub £124k over 2 years; Worcestershire Ultramed £240k over 3 years; NWAFT Ultraprep £223k over 3 years). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/31980e5b-7425-4133-8d72-135bfe8294c1)
- G-Cloud 15 pricing models for pre-op vary: per instance or team (Pathpoint from £48.5k a year), per transaction (AireFrame £2.40; Synopsis £2.90–£3.50 per pre-op; MyPreOp+ £3.13–£6.25 per submission), per patient (Remcare £3–£14 a year) and per specialty (NEC PACT £30k per specialty plus £0.25 per patient, with £20k onboarding). [source](https://assets.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud-15/documents/721733/214669371000433-pricing-document-2026-01-29-1809.pdf)
- NHS SBS's new Patient/Citizen Communication, Engagement & Hybrid Mail framework (SBS10521, £250m) explicitly covers Patient Engagement Portals and surveys, making it a route for questionnaire/engagement products. PAHT has already called off a PEP (Zesty) under it. [source](https://www.sbs.nhs.uk/news/new-250m-communication-framework-launched/)
- NHS SBS cites an estimated £1.2bn a year lost to missed appointments (DNAs) as the driver for its patient communication framework. [source](https://www.sbs.nhs.uk/news/new-250m-communication-framework-launched/)
- LPP plans CDHS 2.0 (about £2.4bn, possibly 8 years), with a contract notice expected early 2027 and a start around Oct 2027. The current CDHS (81 suppliers, single lot, Oct 2024 – Sep 2028) allows direct award from a list-price catalogue and has been used for pre-op SaaS (PAHT Pathpoint). [source](https://www.publictechnology.net/?p=13604)
- NHS England bought a G-Cloud 13 service (Mason Advisory, £272k, Nov 2023 – Mar 2024) for Wayfinder MI/KPI reporting and to set up a PEP supplier onboarding function and governance for NHS App/Wayfinder integration. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/fcbff905-a2f2-4055-b816-d2c895d4a131)
- Commentary (Nelson Advisors, not an NHS England primary source) says NHS England intends to move core appointment functions to the NHS App and disintermediate standalone PEPs (about £11m a year saving). It also says the planned-care pillar includes digital pre-operative questionnaires and that Epic–NHS App direct integration can push pre-assessment forms. [source](https://www.healthcare.digital/single-post/the-disintermediation-of-patient-portals-in-england-the-nhs-app-direct-epr-integrations-and-digita)
- Trust PEP specifications now require NHS App sign-in and Wayfinder surfacing of appointments, letters, forms and results, plus clinical questionnaires linked to the EPR (HIOW PEP pre-tender, £800k). [source](https://stotles.com/explore/notices/ac970a7a-6082-4bf9-88b7-1a4df9ee7620/patient-engagement-portal-pep)
- The NHS England national PROMs/registries platform (ORCA) is on a two-year transition contract with NEC (£4.16m to Sep 2027), and a replacement procurement is intended in 2026. This is a national PROMs opportunity adjacent to pre-op. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/7bbd2af5-5357-4ccc-94a3-e9db8dac59a9)
- Digital consent is bought through several routes: G-Cloud 13 (Barts/NEL with Concentric, £45k a year), NOE CPC TTS via Softcat (PAHT with Concentric), a DPS (NUH with EIDO) and an open tender (South Tees Digital Consent and SDM, £135k, start Jan 2027). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/eadc1d97-036c-4b83-b923-8e6fe0608719)
- The NHS SBS TECS2 remote monitoring framework (£150m, 19 suppliers, six lots) was extendable to January 2027, so a successor is due. It is relevant to post-discharge remote monitoring modules. [source](https://htn.co.uk/2023/03/27/nhs-sbs-updates-remote-patient-monitoring-procurement-framework/)
- Digital Health & Care Wales plans one all-Wales pre-operative digital system (£5m excl. VAT, 2027-2032, extendable to 2034) with health screening at listing, risk stratification, remote completion, digital inclusion and structured data for national repositories. A tender notice was expected 1 May 2026 but has not appeared on FTS. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/021393-2026)
- Royal Surrey's £300k electronic POA tender weights scripted demonstrations at 25%, equal to technical response and price. Requirement-spec compliance is 15% and social value 10%. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/073826-2026)
- NHS Scotland's 2023 PIN combined a national pre-op assessment online triage tool (remote questionnaire, staged patient support, clinician triage, EPR integration) with theatre scheduling across 381 theatres. Only theatre scheduling went to contract on FTS (Infix Support, £6.3m). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007268-2023)
- London North West University Healthcare awarded a digital pre-operative assessment platform contract in March 2022 (before the window): £52,780 against a £150,000 estimate, 7 tenders, quality 70/price 30. No successor procurement was found on FTS, so the account may be due for renewal. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/007921-2022)
- The All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, £11.9m, concluded 13 Oct 2023, 3+1 years) is at or near expiry, which points to a Welsh re-procurement in 2026-27. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/032382-2023)
- Bradford and Airedale re-tendered their patient experience portal in July 2026 (£4.33m) after the Dec 2025 award to Zesty, Xerox and Oracle. The minimum scope includes digital forms and waiting list validation, native Oracle EPR integration, and alignment with the NHS App and Patient Care Aggregator (Wayfinder). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/070821-2026)
- Warrington and Halton required its patient engagement portal to exchange data with the EPR through bi-directional interfaces and open APIs and to integrate with the NHS App and NHS login (DrDoctor, £2.24m, 2024). [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/004133-2024)
- King's College Hospital and Guy's and St Thomas' plan a £3.75m patient communication and engagement contract (SMS, portal, hybrid mail, chatbot, appointment management) integrated with Epic, framed around the elective backlog. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/034123-2025)
- United Lincolnshire has a £7m pipeline notice for a patient engagement portal and hybrid mail, 2028-2032 (extendable to 2035), expected to go through an NHS framework. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/048809-2026)
- A signed G-Cloud 14 eConsent call-off (EIDO at Countess of Chester) shows typical hospital SaaS terms: about £15k a year licence plus £5k deployment, unlimited users and SMS, EPR demographics pull and write-back, SSO, the Buyer as data controller under UK GDPR, and Cyber Essentials on request. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/A-18118)
- Trust-level PROMs contracts are small, from about GBP 12k a year to GBP 150k over 3 years. They are often bought by single tender action or DPS/framework call-off, with annual renewals. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/2bdf583c-7316-46af-8bd1-59c645ecee89)
- Wales buys PROMs nationally through the NWSSP All Wales PROMs framework (5 suppliers, GBP 11.9m, concluded 13 Oct 2023, 3+1 years) aligned to the WViHC PROMs Standard Operating Model. By my inference the framework is due for renewal around Oct 2026–Oct 2027. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/032382-2023)
- NHS Commercial Solutions' replacement Patient & Healthcare Communications framework (GBP 1.4bn, 2025–2033) includes Lot 11 'Streamlined Patient Pathways/flow' and Lot 12 'AI-enabled Digital Care systems'. These are routes to market for patient-facing pathway tools. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/4b01b246-d069-49ec-ab9a-d2be725791e1)
- The patient-app minimum spec in the NHSE SACT ePROMs contract lists essentials buyers expect: iOS, Android and PC access, NHS App compatibility, published DPIA, Edge browser support, no Google Cloud storage (IG/DaAG), quick PROM form edits, reminders, carer sharing, block pricing, DTAC/ISO/GDPR. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/Attachment/6b88f2b0-2890-4213-99c5-bcc59d54e570)
- NHSGGC raised its Doccla virtual ward contract from GBP 307k to GBP 3.93m by modification for scale-up. RPM contracts often grow after award without new competition. [source](https://www.publiccontractsscotland.gov.uk/search/show/search_view.aspx?ID=SEP538698)
- UHB/BSol's GBP 1.67m Integrated Patient Pathway tender was abandoned in Dec 2025 because NHSE funding conditions needed material changes. A re-launch is likely. Its award criteria were Technical 70%, Social Value 20%, Presentation 10%. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-05a274)
- Royal Surrey's 2026 open pre-op tender weights scripted demonstrations at 25%, equal to price (25%) and technical response (25%), with requirement specification 15% and social value 10%. Buyers now score live demos heavily. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsRecordPackages/ocds-h6vhtk-06d687)
- Somerset FT governors paper (19 Feb 2024): the board approved year-1 funding in June 2023 for a perioperative screening and optimisation service. Phases were funded at GBP 81k (21/22), GBP 145k (22/23) and GBP 320k (23/24, mainly staff), and a dedicated Digital Nurse Lead was funded. Digital POAC (Pathpoint) is the screening front end. Pre-op software is bought as part of a wider perioperative optimisation business case, not standalone. [source](https://www.somersetft.nhs.uk/about-us/wp-content/uploads/sites/148/2024/02/Strategy-and-Planning-Monday-19-February-2024.pdf)
- Open Medical's SBRI-backed case study (June 2025, West Hertfordshire data from Jun 2024 to May 2025) claims GBP 78,633 savings and about 1,561 avoided in-person visits. The gains come from complexity stratification and from extending POA validity from 3 to 6 months for ASA I-II patients. Vendors now sell on carbon and validity-extension benefits. [source](https://sbrihealthcare.co.uk/impact-case-studies/case-studies/open-medical-electronic-preoperative-assessment-epoa-module)
- Most digital POA buys found are small framework call-offs (G-Cloud 13, DWS2, CDHS Integrated Health Economy, NOE TTS), often through resellers such as Softcat. Many are annual renewals (UHD, PAHT, QEH), so switching windows recur each year. Values range from about GBP 50k to 240k. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/eaf07c0f-bc5e-41f5-9c7f-61df23e5a733)
- Royal Surrey's 2026 open ePOA tender gives 25% of the score to scripted demonstrations, 25% to the technical response, 15% to the requirement specification, 25% to price and 10% to social value. Demo performance carries as much weight as price. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/procurement/ocds-h6vhtk-06d687)
- Worcestershire Acute appears to have moved its digital pre-op solution from Vitalhub (Synopsis, bridging contract Feb-Oct 2024) to Ultramed (Nov 2024-Oct 2027, GBP 240k). This is inferred from two consecutive Contracts Finder awards. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/Notice/078e71a4-a875-4102-9f3c-9bc8d6f527f8)
- Route to market: the Countess of Chester F075 National Data Validation Services framework (est. £10m, 2025-05-04 to 2029-05-03) is the main vehicle for RTT/PTL validation. It explicitly ties validation to PAS-to-EPR migration and to building in-house central validation and booking teams. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/000142-2025)
- Route to market: the LPP Clinical Digital Health Solutions (CDHS) framework is used for direct awards of validation (NUH, NECS LUNA) and for whole EPRs (Royal Orthopaedic Hospital, InterSystems, £13,147,716 over 10 years from 2026-02-26). [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/eb21056c-6ba3-4bb5-96b6-dcb409cb1f5f)
- Route to market: NHS SBS Patient/Citizen Communication, Engagement and Hybrid Mail Solutions framework (SBS10521, £250m ex VAT, 2026-01-07 to 2030-01-06). Lot 1 covers patient portals, AI and appointment management; Lot 7 covers combined solutions. Portal-bundled validation and digital forms are likely to be bought here. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/017717-2025)
- Policy driver: NHS England (via the Strategy Unit and MLCSU) commissioned research on 'Minimum standards for patients and carers on an NHS waiting list' (Ipsos, £93,441, Oct 2025 to Jan 2026). This signals forthcoming national standards for waiting-list communication and support. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/876502b1-85a8-4db3-b4aa-8d802419a5ce)
- HQIP re-procured the National Clinical Audit of Perioperative Care (England and Wales, plus Jersey): 3 years from 2025-08-01, maximum £1,110,000 ex VAT, with an option of 2 more years. It is a national perioperative data driver. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/27857701-afac-4b7c-8b59-e97210ecc913)
- Buyer pattern: waiting well and pre-surgery optimisation is mostly bought as community and VCSE services under the PSR or light-touch rules, often by direct award, with small values (£30k-£300k). Newcastle's programme targets pre-assessment postponements, on-the-day cancellations and failed day cases via diabetes, opiate, smoking and obesity interventions. [source](https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages/054707-2025)
- Theatre productivity is also bought as consultancy: Gloucestershire Hospitals awarded 'Management Consultancy Theatres' to Akeso & Co twice in 2026 (£49,000 and £49,080) via CCS RM6309 MCF4 Lot 7. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/038c0871-6959-4e6a-9116-7647b10fc251)
- Adjacent pre-operative digital tooling: Northumbria awarded orthopaedic pre-operative templating software to Brainlab (£84,804.90, 2025-01-14 to 2028-01-13) via the NHS Supply Chain Surgical Navigation Systems framework, after a 2024 open tender that required calibrated, infection-control-compliant measurement. [source](https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/api/rest/2/get_published_notice/json/ec9a4f28-11cc-4eb9-9a90-827c0a093b7c)

## 11. Why standalone pre-op tenders look like a UK thing

Added 2026-10-23. **Scope note:** this research covered the UK, Ireland and Europe only. **The US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand were not researched**, so this report says nothing about demand there.

Europe does buy: 145 of the 311 counted records are from the rest of Europe, against 152 from the UK. What is rare in Europe is a **stand-alone pre-op assessment tender**. Only a handful were found: AZORG in Belgium (live), Mannheim in Germany (direct award to Novacair), Strasbourg in France, and ULS Alentejo and ULS Entre Douro e Vouga in Portugal (UpHill). The evidence points to six reasons.

1. **Pre-op is bought inside the hospital record (EPR).** Dutch and Belgian hospitals run pre-op screening in their EPR. Diakonessenhuis uses ChipSoft HiX triage: the questionnaire gives a provisional ASA score, ASA 1-2 patients are assessed digitally, and 55% of screenings have been fully digital since Feb 2024 [link](https://www.conclusion.com/en-nl/cases/diakonessenhuis-digitises-preoperative-screening). MUMC+ bought Epic for 10 years, so its pre-op tooling is decided inside that programme [link](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/293380). AZ Jan Palfijn Gent bought an integrated HiX EPR (EUR 117.6m, 10 years), so pre-op there will default to HiX [link](https://ted.europa.eu/nl/notice/-/detail/646663-2026). The UK has EPR-native pre-op as well (for example Epic MyChart at Birmingham Women's and Children's) [link](https://bwc.nhs.uk/mychart-bwc), but many English trusts still buy pre-op as its own product.
2. **Many buys are never published.** Dutch general hospitals are not bound by procurement law; the UMCG notice says so for OZG and Treant [link](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/395484). So only the university hospitals publish, and Dutch general-hospital pre-op buys (Treant is shown as a NovaCair E-POS customer) never reach TenderNed [link](https://www.dutchitchannel.nl/news/730331/chipsoft-verliest-hoger-beroep-over-regionaal-pati%C3%ABntendossier). In Spain, single hospitals use minor contracts under EUR 15k: La Paz bought PROMs/PREMs as annual EUR 14,700 contracts [link](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/contrato/D540_8933), and Madrid hospitals trial AI scheduling and pre-op tools the same way [link](https://contratos-publicos.comunidad.madrid/contrato/D1452_2895).
3. **In Germany, pre-op sits inside patient-portal buys funded by the KHZG.** KHZG funding category 2 (patient portals) pays for digital admission, history-taking and consent. Havelland's portal tender required home completion of history, condition and medication questionnaires [link](https://www.heuking.de/de/anwaelte/profil/projekte/projekt/beschaffung-und-einfuehrung-eines-patientenportals.html). Doctolib and Thieme sell the portal together with digital history-taking, education and consent [link](https://www.zwp-online.info/zwpnews/wirtschaft-und-recht/businessnews/doctolib-und-der-software-e-consentpro-von-thieme-kooperieren). Portal tenders gate bidders on references with the hospital's main clinical system (ORBIS, NEXUS) [link](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/444820-2025/xml).
4. **Direct awards to incumbents are common.** Mannheim used a direct-award notice (VEAT) for pre-op to Novacair [link](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/728166-2025/xml). German university hospitals repeatedly direct-award sqior's theatre assistant on exclusivity grounds [link](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/572086-2026/xml). Amsterdam UMC and AP-HP bought recovery apps by direct award [link](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/-/detail/70081-2026). Thieme's consent product is mostly extended by VEATs [link](https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/705344-2024/xml).
5. **The clinical model differs.** Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis screens mainly by a 10-20 minute phone call [link](https://www.jeroenboschziekenhuis.nl/afdelingen/preoperatieve-screening-pos/pdf). AZORG sends patients to their GP for pre-op tests, using the national KCE guidance, and its new tender would bring this in-house and online [link](https://www.azorg.be/nl/professional/huisartsen/preoperatieve-medicatie-onderzoeken).
6. **The UK has a national push and publishes small buys.** NHS England's five core requirements expect early screening, 3-monthly contact and optimisation [link](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/earlier-screening-risk-assessment-and-health-optimisation-in-perioperative-pathways/). The NHS Standard Contract makes this a duty for acute providers [link](https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/25-nhssc-fl-scs-2526-2627-comp.pdf). GIRFT has pre-op guidance [link](https://gettingitrightfirsttime.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/GIRFT-Pre-operative-assessment-guidance-FINAL-V1-July-2023.pdf). The planning framework puts pre- and post-appointment questionnaires in the NHS App by 2028/29 [link](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/medium-term-planning-framework-delivering-change-together-2026-27-to-2028-29/). English trusts also publish even small framework call-offs on Contracts Finder, so the UK market is easier to see, not only bigger.

**What this means for selling in Europe (our recommendation):**
- Sell as a **module that plugs into the EPR**, not as a stand-alone system. NovaCair connects to HiX through ChipSoft's Zorgplatform: a completed questionnaire creates a worklist task, and the report opens from HiX [link](https://novacair.com/koppelingen/chipsoft/). Dutch Epic hospitals are moving to an API platform [link](https://www.tenderned.nl/aankondigingen/overzicht/353322).
- In Germany, **partner with a portal supplier** rather than bid against KHZG portals.
- Dutch general hospitals can buy **without a tender**, so they are a sales-led market (direct approach, pilots), not a tender market.
- Bid the visible tenders where they appear (AZORG; university hospitals), with CE marking, ISO 27001 and local-language content, as Mannheim required.

**Not researched:** the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. They need their own live research run before any claim about them.
